_meta.purpose: Durable hand-researched overlay merged into draft-board.json by build-draft-board.mjs. Survives ADP rebuilds. Web-sourced 2026-07-20; re-verify injury/flag status in the final 2 weeks before draft.
_meta.risk_flags_semantics: true = documented exposure; false = researched, no current exposure; researched:true means it was checked. Clean designation = not surfaced in the league-wide suspension/holdout sweep AND clean games-played, a reasonable confidence level, not a per-player deep dive.
_meta.injury_history_null: rookies / <1 NFL season: no history exists; page shows 'no data' rather than a guess
_meta.scouting_seed: Top-tier scouting_brief seed (13 players by ADP), web-sourced 2026-07-21. Scheme-fit-first prose + role_stability/scheme_fit/override_flag. Retrieval-grounded; extend deeper as the draft nears. null below = not scouted yet.

scouting_brief.rationale: Retired since the 2021 NFL season; not an active 2026 player. His appearance in the pool is a search-rank/roster artifact, not a scoutable player, so there are no current sources and nothing to scout.

scouting_brief.prose: The locked Rams starter, on a modified camp schedule as HC Sean McVay rests him (he skips some practice days for "his own independent stuff") after a back injury cost him all of 2025 camp before an MVP-caliber season. McVay says he is "as healthy as he's been at this point in the calendar in a few years." A locked QB in a strong McVay passing game; the standing watch is age and the back, not the job.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked LAR starter on a managed camp schedule after a 2025 back issue; healthy now, coming off an MVP-type year.

NFL.com — Stafford (back) to work out, could practice

scouting_brief.prose: The unquestioned Chiefs starter at 36 in Year 14, but HC Andy Reid is openly managing his practice reps ("you have to fight him to get him off the field"), a rotation about age rather than a demotion. Kelce came back focused after mulling retirement and Reid says he is "playing like crazy," though last year's drops resurfaced (a camp drop turned into an interception). A locked TE1 whose real risk is age-driven decline and target erosion behind Mahomes' younger receivers, not his job.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked KC starter, but Reid is age-managing his snaps at 36; the risk is decline and drops, not the role.

sources.label: Andy Reid on managing Kelce's camp reps

2133.injury_history: Missed time 2024-25 (14/14); age 33. Decline + durability is the compound risk.
2133.adp_commentary: WR at ~55. Name value; an age-33 WR is a steep redraft bet and the board rates him below ADP, a fade in this ceiling-over-name format.

scouting_brief.prose: Matthew Stafford's red-zone target magnet. He led the NFL in receiving touchdowns (14) and red-zone targets in his first Rams season while operating on a moderate 22-24% target share, finishing a top-10 half-PPR receiver on scoring rather than volume. The obvious caveat is touchdown regression (don't bake in 14 scores), and he's 33. But the defined role in a strong McVay offense holds a WR2 floor; projections peg him around 75-928-10.
scouting_brief.rationale: Stafford's red-zone target magnet (led NFL in RZ targets + rec TDs in 2025); TD regression is coming, but the defined role holds WR2 value (age 33 the cap).

2216.injury_history: Age-33 season coming off injuries and his worst fantasy year (10.6 PPG, WR41); 1.62 YPRR is a separate red flag. Durability plus age-decline is the compound risk.
2216.adp_commentary: WR at ~57. Name value on an age-33 receiver coming off his worst season and now in a new SF role; the board likely rates him below ADP. A fade in this ceiling-over-name format.

scouting_brief.prose: Signed by San Francisco to be the prime WR1, demoting Ricky Pearsall, and the target tree is wide open for him to become Brock Purdy's primary option in the red zone. The profile mirrors Davante Adams: a touchdown-driven WR2 with spike weeks and quiet weeks. The caps are age (33) and a chronic hamstring history: injuries limited him to eight games in 2025, the fifth straight year with a hamstring issue, though he posted a 24.4% target share when he did play.
scouting_brief.rationale: Signed as SF's prime WR1 (demoting Pearsall) with an open target tree for Purdy; TD/red-zone upside, but age 33 + a chronic hamstring history are real caps.

sources.label: SI (owners lick chops at SF signing)

scouting_brief.prose: The Commanders' new WR2 opposite Terry McLaurin under OC David Blough (the former backup QB promoted into the role this offseason), running zone-savvy underneath routes that HC Dan Quinn specifically credited (Aug. 11) with adding 'explosive play passes' to the offense — Quinn praised his zone recognition and ability to 'sit down' against it, plus solid releases in man coverage. Camp reports (Aug. 7-11) have his workload deliberately ramped slowly as he learns the playbook, with extra post-practice route-detail work alongside Jayden Daniels; real in-game chemistry is still building rather than proven. Coming off a healthy but wildly inconsistent 2025 (WR17, sub-10.4 fantasy points in nearly half his games), age and that week-to-week volatility remain the caps on a defined but still-developing role.
scouting_brief.rationale: HC Dan Quinn's Aug. 11 on-record praise (zone savvy, explosive-play add) is the first coach-level confirmation of Diggs' fit; upgrades scheme_fit from neutral to plus.

scouting_brief.prose: The locked Lions starter, adjusting to new OC and playcaller Drew Petzing (his fourth coordinator since 2021), who is installing a more run-first, balanced attack with heavy 13-personnel looks. Goff says the scheme is "tailored to the guys we have" and has come together nicely in camp, and the weapons stay elite (Gibbs extended, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, LaPorta). A locked QB; the only watch is a modest passing-volume dip in a run-leaning scheme.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked DET starter under new OC Drew Petzing's run-first scheme; elite weapons intact, a slight passing-volume dip the only risk.

sources.label: DetroitLions.com — Goff talks new offense under Petzing
SI On SI Lions — Goff open to preseason snaps

3198.injury_history: Remarkably durable (17/17/17); the flag is age (32), not health.
3198.adp_commentary: RB at ~22. An age-32 RB is the archetypal cliff bet, but his workload and BAL offense have shown no decline; the board rates him a clear RB1 and the durability is a genuine plus.

scouting_brief.prose: Still Baltimore's workhorse and still elite by Next Gen Stats after a 1,595-yard, 16-TD, 307-carry 2025, with Lamar Jackson keeping defenses honest. The case against is age and mileage: he enters his age-32 season with 2,800+ career touches, where aging curves say decline is overdue, and a new coaching staff plus a remade interior offensive line add uncertainty. He's defied the curve so far and stayed durable (17 games three years running); analysts still peg him a mid-to-late first-round RB1.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked workhorse, still elite by NGS; age-32 + 2,800 career touches + a new staff/remade interior O-line are the caps, but he's defied the aging curve and stayed durable.

scouting_brief.prose: Drake Maye's most-trusted target and just extended (two years, up to $20M) mid-camp, coming off a career-best 2025 (60-768-7). New England added A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs at receiver, but Maye's chemistry with Brown is still developing while the Henry-Maye connection is proven, so Henry stays featured in the near term. A locked TE1 whose cap is the crowded new receiver room eventually thinning his target share.
scouting_brief.rationale: Extended, Maye's proven top target; the new Brown/Doubs WRs are a longer-term target-share cap, not a near-term threat.

sources.label: ESPN — Patriots TE Henry agrees to extension

3294.injury_history: 2024 catastrophic hamstring (torn off the bone, Week 8, season-ending surgery; 8 games). Returned fully in 2025 (17 games, Comeback Player of the Year finalist).
3294.adp_commentary: QB at ~97.8. The 2024 injury is fully behind him (a healthy 17-game 2025 proves it); with the offense intact he's a solid streaming-plus QB, though the 1-QB caveat applies.

scouting_brief.prose: Coming off a top-seven finish (4,552 yards, 30 TDs, 21.9 points per game) with one of the league's best receiver duos in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, both 1,000-yard players. He is a locked starter and a mid-round QB1 value. For this format the ceiling is tempered: he is a pocket passer with no rushing, so the 4-point passing-TD scoring taxes his strength, and two alpha mouths to feed can cap the weekly high end. A steady, unspectacular QB1 here.
scouting_brief.rationale: Top-7 finish and an elite WR duo, but a pocket passer in a 4-pt-pass-TD, no-rush format and a two-alpha target split keep him a middling QB1.

scouting_brief.prose: Signed with the Chargers on a one-year deal after nine years in Cleveland, but he profiles as the third tight end behind breakout second-year Oronde Gadsden (the clear primary) and blocking-first Charlie Kolar in Mike McDaniel's offense. He is coming off an injury-marred 2025 (24.4 yards per game) and projects for limited, mostly complementary snaps. A deep-league dart whose upside grows only if Gadsden slips or McDaniel leans on two-TE sets for Herbert.
scouting_brief.rationale: The third TE behind Gadsden and Kolar in LA after an injury-hit year; a deep-league option unless Gadsden slips.

4034.injury_history: 2024 lost 13 games to bilateral Achilles tendinitis (soft-tissue, both legs) + late PCL sprain; answered with a 17-game RB1 season in 2025. Age 30 + Achilles history is the recurrence/decline risk, not a current injury.
4034.adp_commentary: Market drafts him ~RB5 (ADP 5.7) while the board values him ~RB9. You're paying up for ceiling against an age-30, Achilles-history availability cap. A slight reach at cost in a format where RB-adjacent value is available later.

scouting_brief.prose: Still the centerpiece of Kyle Shanahan's offense under second-year OC Klay Kubiak, a system built around his three-down rush/receiving versatility. He sat out Monday (Aug. 10) with 'tightness' the team is framing as scheduled load management, not a new injury: Kubiak said 'He's a little sore, but he's doing fine, so we'll just kind of manage him as we go.' Sentiment stays split on the 30-year-old coming off 413 touches — Fansided's Christopher Kline (Aug. 10) urges caution given the roughly 48% average decline rate for backs who cross 370 touches, while most outlets still treat him as a top-5 pick on receiving floor alone. Watch whether the 'maintenance day' framing becomes a recurring pattern.
scouting_brief.rationale: Scheme fit and role unchanged; a single planned rest day is workload management, not a new role signal, and the age/workload risk was already priced in.

scouting_brief.prose: At 31 and coming off the least efficient season of his career, Kamara restructured to stay in New Orleans but now takes a backseat to Travis Etienne (signed to a four-year, $52M deal), with the two splitting first-team reps in camp. His receiving edge is slipping (career-low efficiency) and his durability is a concern (13 games missed over three years). A committee back not worth drafting before Round 11.
scouting_brief.rationale: Ceding the NO lead to Etienne at 31 after his least efficient year; a fading committee back with slipping receiving value.

4037.injury_history: 2024 season-ending dislocated/fractured ankle that also delayed and wrecked 2025 (9 PPG over injury-hit games). ~30 games missed across 9 seasons. Reportedly enters 2026 healthy.
4037.adp_commentary: WR at ~93. Was a 19.7-PPG player before the ankle; if fully healthy that's a massive value at WR36 ADP, but the ankle wrecked a year-plus and the durability history is long. A high-variance value pick.

scouting_brief.prose: Healthy again and the favorite for Tampa Bay's slot role, with Emeka Egbuka and Jalen McMillan outside and Mike Evans gone to San Francisco, so there is a vacated WR1 target load to chase. The offense runs through Baker Mayfield, and Godwin remains a plus PPR option from the slot when right. Two caps: he is 30 and has played just 16 games total across the last two seasons (ankle), and he shares the alpha role with the ascending Egbuka. A WR4/flex with more upside in PPR if he stays on the field.
scouting_brief.rationale: Healthy slot role with Evans gone gives PPR value, but age 30, a two-year injury run and sharing the alpha role with Egbuka cap him at WR4/flex.

4046.injury_history: 2025 torn ACL + LCL (Week 15). Throwing this offseason and targeting Week 1, but KC has stopped short of guaranteeing that date. Real Week-1 risk on a structural knee.
4046.adp_commentary: QB at ~101. Name-brand QB coming off a torn ACL+LCL with an uncertain Week 1; in a 1-QB streaming league there is no reason to pay QB1-name prices for that risk. Let someone else.

scouting_brief.prose: Unquestioned franchise QB in Andy Reid's offense, so the only real variables are his own health and a reshuffled pass-catcher group. Mahomes is rehabbing a left knee injury but has shown improved mobility rolling both directions in camp, and he is working with projected starters Rashee Rice (on a managed workload after a knee issue), Xavier Worthy, Tyquan Thornton, Travis Kelce and new RB Kenneth Walker III. A locked QB1 whose weekly ceiling tracks how fast Rice and the young receivers round into form.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked KC starter; health and a reshuffled WR corps (Rice managed, Worthy, Walker III) are the only variables.

sources.label: SI On SI Chiefs — Day 4 camp, offense averts crisis
ESPN — what we're seeing at Chiefs camp

scouting_brief.prose: Limited to three games in 2025 by a foot injury and now, at 31, buried in a rebuilt Arizona backfield behind rookie Jeremiyah Love (No. 3 overall pick) and Tyler Allgeier. Conner profiles as the RB3 and could be traded or released to find a fit. A late-round reserve whose standalone value depends on injuries ahead of him.
scouting_brief.rationale: A 31-year-old coming off a foot injury and buried behind Love and Allgeier in ARI; an RB3 reserve barring a change of scenery.

4199.injury_history: 2025 limited to 12 games (combination of injuries incl. a Week 18 hip); age 31. Age + accumulating soft-tissue is the profile.

notes: Restructured to stay in MIN for 2026.

4199.adp_commentary: RB at ~107. An aging back in a timeshare with Jordan Mason; little upside unless injury clears the way. Depth/bye filler at cost.

scouting_brief.prose: Back in Minnesota on a restructured deal and, at 31, again splitting a timeshare with Jordan Mason. Jones keeps the passing-down role (Mason has almost no receiving history), which gives him the higher PPR floor of the two, but Mason pushes him for early-down and goal-line work. He is coming off an injury-plagued season with near career lows across efficiency metrics. A low-end RB3/flex, best in PPR.
scouting_brief.rationale: Keeps the passing-down role in a timeshare with Mason, but age 31, injury risk and a shrinking early-down share cap him at an RB3/flex.

4217.injury_history: MAJOR: ruptured his Achilles on Jan 11 2026. Likely opens on Reserve/PUP and misses ~the first month; turns 33 in October. A fringe-TE1 finish would be 'borderline miraculous' per analysts.
4217.adp_commentary: TE at ~99. Do not draft as a starter. A ruptured Achilles at 33 with real PUP/first-month risk makes him a late-round stash for the playoff run at best, not the every-week TE1 his name implies. You (ThatWasButtery) rostered him in 2025. This is a clear sell/avoid at cost.

scouting_brief.prose: The bet is entirely health: Kittle tore his right Achilles in January's playoff win and opened camp on PUP, though he says he is 'on track' for Week 1. When right he is a top-five tight end, but the recovery timeline plus a reshaped San Francisco pecking order (Mike Evans and Christian McCaffrey ahead of him for targets) push his projection to the TE9 to TE13 range. A high-upside pick with real early-season risk of missed time or reduced form.
scouting_brief.rationale: Elite when healthy, but an Achilles rehab (PUP to open camp) and a target pecking order behind Evans/McCaffrey cloud the early season.

4866.injury_history: Durable recently (14/16/16), no chronic pattern; the flag is age (29) not health.
4866.adp_commentary: RB at ~15.4. Age-29 RBs are the classic cliff risk, but the PHI O-line + recent workload keep him a fringe RB1. Fair, not a bargain.

scouting_brief.prose: Bell-cow role locked (79% snap share, 70% of the rush attempts in 2025), and new OC Sean Mannion is expected to put Hurts under center more often, a wrinkle Barkley says he's eager for and one the numbers suggest boosts his efficiency. The 2025 dip tracked an offensive line that fell from 9th to 16th in run-block win rate; a healthy line plus the scheme tweak point to a bounce-back. Age 29 and the 2024 workload are the only real caps; consensus has him mid-first to early-second.
scouting_brief.rationale: Bell-cow role locked; Mannion's under-center scheme + a healthy O-line point to a bounce-back, age-29 the only cap.

4881.adp_commentary: QB at ~39.6. The format's premium QB archetype (rushing floor immune to the 4-pt passing-TD cap). Same 1-QB caveat: the streamer band is free, so pay only for the ceiling.

scouting_brief.prose: The premier rushing-QB archetype this format prizes, but 2025 was a warning: hamstring and back injuries cost four games and cratered his rushing (67 carries, 349 yards, 2 rushing TDs; career lows), dropping him to QB16. A new OC in Declan Doyle and a revamped, rookie-heavy receiver corps add scheme uncertainty. Durability is now a real concern (four-plus games missed in three of five years); a healthy rebound is the high-end QB1 case, but no longer a given.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked franchise konami QB (the rushing profile is the format's edge), but 2025's injury-driven rushing collapse + a new OC cap a health-dependent rebound.

scouting_brief.prose: The locked Buccaneers starter, now under new OC Zac Robinson (in from Atlanta), whose scheme leans on pre-snap movement and a stronger ground game to revive an offense that finished 21st in 2025. Mayfield has thrown well in camp and predicted a strong campaign. A locked QB whose ceiling rides on the new scheme clicking and his pass-catchers staying healthy.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked TB starter under new OC Zac Robinson's movement/run-leaning scheme; back-end QB1 if it clicks.

sources.label: Last Word on Sports — Bucs camp, offense poised for revival

scouting_brief.prose: Posts strong real-life efficiency (top-five in success rate and completion over expected in 2025) but finished only QB25, a low ceiling for a relatively immobile passer in the league's seventh-most run-heavy offense. He has a deep cast (Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp, Rashid Shaheed, A.J. Barner) but a new playcaller in Fleury replaces the easy answers of Kubiak's play-action scheme. A one-QB-league streamer, not a target.
scouting_brief.rationale: Efficient but immobile in a run-heavy offense that capped him at QB25; a streamer whose ceiling the format and scheme both limit.

scouting_brief.prose: Traded from Chicago to Buffalo as Josh Allen's new WR1 and reunited with Joe Brady, the setup for a bounce-back. He's the favorite to lead the Bills in targets, and analysts see a path back to a 25%+ share (roughly 125-150 Allen targets) after four straight 24%+ seasons before 2025. Allen called him a 'seamless fit.' The cap is Buffalo's run-lean, spread-it-around offense (Shakir, Kincaid, Cook), which trims raw volume.
scouting_brief.rationale: Josh Allen's new WR1 after the CHI->BUF trade (reunited with Joe Brady); a 25%+ target share is the case, Buffalo's run-lean the cap.

sources.label: CBS Sports (Bills trade for DJ Moore)

4984.adp_commentary: QB1 at ~24.2, but in a 1-QB, 10-team league QB13-16 stream free all year. The board's VORP likes the player, not the pick: only worth it if you value his konami-rushing floor over the RB/WR you'd pass at that slot.

scouting_brief.prose: The exact QB profile this format prizes: three straight seasons of 500+ rushing yards and 12+ rushing touchdowns, and no worse than the overall QB2 in points per game over that span, a rushing floor immune to the league's 4-point passing-TD cap. Buffalo has leaned more run-heavy (sub-4,000 passing two years running) but added DJ Moore to a group with Khalil Shakir, Dalton Kincaid and a league-leading rusher in James Cook. Locked franchise QB, konami-ideal scheme.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked franchise QB; his rushing floor is exactly the konami edge this format rewards, and DJ Moore adds pass-game juice.

scouting_brief.prose: A reliable underneath option for C.J. Stroud who finished TE11 in 2025 (82-777-3), but the volume that carried him is at risk. Houston added Foster Moreau and drafted Max Klare, and a healthier Cade Stover crowds the tight end room, while Schultz's lack of big-play ability (7.0 yards per target for his career) leaves him volume-dependent. A midrange TE2 you settle for after Round 11.
scouting_brief.rationale: Reliable Stroud target off a TE11 year, but added TE competition (Moreau, Klare) and a low-aDOT profile leave him a volume-dependent TE2.

scouting_brief.prose: Now the unquestioned Ravens tight end after Isaiah Likely left in free agency, which removes the committee that capped him and should push his target share back up in Lamar Jackson's offense. Andrews is healthy, re-signed (three years, $39.3M) as Lamar's guy, and the rookies behind him (Hibner, Cuevas) are depth rather than competition. A locked TE1 whose only real caps are age (30, ninth season) and Baltimore's run-heavy script.
scouting_brief.rationale: Likely's departure makes Andrews the clear BAL TE1 again; target share should rise, with age and the run-heavy script the only caps.

sources.label: Russell Street Report — Ravens camp notes

scouting_brief.prose: The clear Eagles TE1 and a primary beneficiary of A.J. Brown's trade to New England, which vacates targets alongside DeVonta Smith and rookie Makai Lemon, while new OC Sean Mannion runs a scheme that has historically featured tight ends. Hurts and Goedert have connected often in camp on underneath, chain-moving and red-zone work off a career-high 11-TD 2025. A locked starter whose only real risk is his injury history, not his role.
scouting_brief.rationale: Clear PHI TE1; Brown's exit and a TE-friendly new OC (Mannion) point up, with durability the only cap.

sources.label: NBC Sports Philadelphia — most important: Goedert

scouting_brief.prose: Was the unquestioned WR1 for Bo Nix the last two years (WR18 then WR24 in points per game), but Jaylen Waddle's arrival reshapes the room: the passing game is expected to condense around Waddle and Sutton, with Sutton in the secondary role at age 31. He keeps real red-zone value (nine TDs on 38 red-zone targets since Nix took over). Declining efficiency and the new competition, in an offense with essentially no vacated volume, point to a volume-dependent WR3.
scouting_brief.rationale: Still a starter and red-zone target, but Waddle's arrival pushes him to the No. 2 role at 31; a volume-dependent WR3 with a lower ceiling.

scouting_brief.prose: A bounce-back bargain: his down 2025 (51-438-3) came on subpar quarterbacking, and the Kyler Murray addition is a real upgrade (Murray helped Trey McBride finish as fantasy's TE2 in 2024). He remains Minnesota's clear TE1. The caps are age-29 athletic decline (career-low 8.6 yards per reception) and a new red-zone competitor in Jauan Jennings. A value at his depressed TE ADP.
scouting_brief.rationale: Clear MIN TE1 whose QB play jumps with Murray (a proven TE elevator); age-related decline and Jennings' red-zone role are the caps.

scouting_brief.prose: Projects again as Pittsburgh's clear No. 1 receiver, and the McCarthy offense should mean more passing volume than Arthur Smith's did last year. Two things cap him. Aaron Rodgers, in what he says is his final season, throws a low average depth of target with dwindling arm strength, which blunts Metcalf's deep game, and the Steelers added Michael Pittman Jr. for competition. His first Pittsburgh year was good-not-great (WR24 in points per game, single-digit outings in six of 15 games). A boom-bust WR3.
scouting_brief.rationale: Clear WR1 role and more McCarthy passing volume, but Rodgers' arm decline plus added competition (Pittman) keep him a boom-bust WR3.

scouting_brief.prose: Traded to Minnesota and set as the Week 1 starter, walking into the best receiving corps of his career (Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings, T.J. Hockenson) under Kevin O'Connell. His legs are the format edge: he has averaged at least 30 rushing yards per game in all seven of his NFL seasons. The watches are a career-low 17.9 points per game in an injury-shortened 2025 and J.J. McCarthy waiting behind him. A late-round QB with real rushing-fueled upside.
scouting_brief.rationale: A proven rushing QB into his best-ever cast under O'Connell; the format rewards the legs, with a benching risk (McCarthy) the only real watch.

5850.injury_history: 2025 knee (missed Weeks 11-12; noticeably less effective after: 14.6 touches/11.3 pts vs 21.1/19.6 before).

notes: Arrested May 27 2026, five charges incl. felony strangulation (alleged domestic, Brown County WI); released same day. DA has NOT decided on charges. Investigation ongoing.
Commissioner-Exempt-list / suspension exposure while unresolved; if charges are declined he'll likely avoid suspension, but this is a live, unresolved legal + availability risk.

5850.adp_commentary: RB at ~25.2. Top-12 RB talent, but a pending domestic-violence case (felony charge, undecided) plus a 2025 knee that sapped his second half make this a genuine avoid-until-clarity at cost. The ADP has not fully absorbed the legal risk.

scouting_brief.prose: On the field he's Green Bay's clear RB1: roughly a 60% rush share with Brooks and Lloyd behind him, and 13+ rushing TDs in each of the last two years in LaFleur's run-friendly, goal-line-heavy scheme. But the overriding 2026 story is off-field: a late-May domestic-abuse arrest (released, insufficient evidence to charge at the time) leaves real availability and discipline exposure, and he projects as the Week-1 starter only if the case doesn't reopen. Role locked; availability is the live question (see risk flags).
scouting_brief.rationale: Football role locked (clear GB RB1, ~60% share, goal-line TDs); the dominant risk is the unresolved legal case / availability, not the role.

5859.injury_history: Missed some time 2024-25 (13/15). Minor hamstring/knee, not chronic.
5859.adp_commentary: WR at ~24.4. Now in New England with Drake Maye (traded from PHI); target dominance intact but the offense downgrade caps the ceiling, a mild reach at ADP 16-range boards, fairer here at 24.

scouting_brief.prose: Now the clear No. 1 for Drake Maye after the trade to New England, and the move reads as a scheme upgrade rather than the downgrade some feared: the Patriots ranked 9th in neutral pass rate (Philly 15th) and 15th in pass rate inside the 10 (Philly 32nd), so his touchdown fuel actually rises, and Maye led the NFL in completion rate and yards per attempt in 2025. Brown has finished top-7 in target share seven straight years; analysts see top-five upside. Role locked, scheme a plus.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked WR1 for Maye; NE is a pass-rate/red-zone upgrade over PHI, more bullish than the standing adp_commentary's 'downgrade' read.

scouting_brief.prose: Was an MVP-caliber surprise before a Week-14 Achilles tear (QB5 through 10 weeks, guiding Indianapolis to 8-2), and he is fully cleared and expects to be 100% for Week 1. The concern is that his value leaned on mobility, and post-Achilles quarterbacks (Rodgers, Cousins) saw efficiency dips, while the Colts will not risk goal-line sneaks on the healing tendon, trimming his rushing-TD upside. A late-round QB (QB27 ADP) with real bounce-back range if the legs return.
scouting_brief.rationale: A pre-injury QB5 pace, but a torn Achilles curtails the mobility his value relied on; a late-round QB whose ceiling rides on the legs returning.

scouting_brief.prose: Back in San Francisco on a one-year deal, returning to Kyle Shanahan's scheme after a season in Washington, and he lands in a real role with Ricky Pearsall out for the year following surgery. Shanahan built much of his offense around manufacturing touches for Deebo's run-after-catch (jet motion, screens, designed runs), and 49ers teammates say they expect "the best version" of him back in a familiar system with Purdy, Kittle and McCaffrey. A versatile gadget-WR whose value rides on how heavily Shanahan features him and his durability at 30.
scouting_brief.rationale: Returned to SF on a 1-yr deal after a year in WAS; Shanahan-scheme fit with Pearsall out opens touches, durability/age the cap.

sources.label: 49ers Webzone — teammates expect the best version of Deebo
NFL.com — Deebo: return to 49ers was 'just a matter of time'

scouting_brief.prose: Traded from Detroit to Houston, which flips his outlook: after three years splitting with Jahmyr Gibbs he steps into the clear early-down and goal-line lead role, with only Woody Marks behind him. The engine of his fantasy value (goal-line work) is intact and could grow. The caps are real, though: he turns 29, Houston's offensive line is weak, and DeMeco Ryans' backfields have produced few rushing TDs (six in 2025). A volume-driven RB2.
scouting_brief.rationale: Traded to Houston as the clear early-down/goal-line lead (Gibbs timeshare over); age 29 + a weak O-line + a low-RB-TD scheme are the caps.

notes: Live training-camp holdout for a new deal (unresolved as of this research). Fined per day; missed-camp/games risk until settled.

5927.adp_commentary: WR at ~58.8. A live holdout depresses the ADP: upside is a solid WR2 if the deal gets done and he reports on time, downside is missed camp and early games. Do not draft until the holdout resolves.

scouting_brief.prose: Holdout resolved (3 years, $97M), which reframes his outlook: his 2025 was wrecked by a holdout-related quad injury (10 games), but he's set for a bounce-back as the undisputed WR1 for Jayden Daniels, with Washington near the top of the league in vacated targets. New OC David Blough has said the plan is to get him 'ten targets a game,' and the depth chart behind him is unproven (Luke McCaffrey, a rookie). Age 31 and Daniels' health are the caps.
scouting_brief.rationale: Holdout resolved (3yr/$97M); undisputed WR1 set for a bounce-back with OC Blough targeting 'ten targets a game' (age 31 and Daniels' health the caps).

scouting_brief.prose: Traded from Las Vegas to Jacksonville at the 2025 deadline and re-signed (three years, $60M), he stepped straight into a major role in Coen's offense and held it even after Brian Thomas Jr. got healthy. He is the steady, high-floor option in the room, Trevor Lawrence's reliable underneath target. The cap is the same crowded target tree that limits everyone here (Thomas, Washington, Travis Hunter), so he profiles as a safe WR3 rather than a ceiling play.
scouting_brief.rationale: High-floor, reliable target who kept his role after Thomas returned, but a crowded JAX room caps him at a safe WR3.

scouting_brief.prose: The clear Tennessee lead back, and new OC Brian Daboll (HC Robert Saleh) has historically ridden a single back. Tyjae Spears and rookie Nicholas Singleton are only minor threats, with Spears' role tilting toward passing-down work. The 2025 counting stats were dragged down by a putrid offense (RB29 in points per game despite a top-17 opportunity share), but added weapons (Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson) and a Year 2 leap from Cam Ward should open more room. A steady RB2.
scouting_brief.rationale: Clear lead back for a Daboll offense that features one RB; an improved supporting cast around Cam Ward points to steady RB2 volume.

6770.injury_history: 2025 limited to 8 games (turf-toe surgery). When healthy a top-5 fantasy QB, but that version has shown up once in three seasons; the injury history is the story.
6770.adp_commentary: QB at ~58. Elite ceiling with Chase + Higgins, but in this 1-QB streaming league you pay only for the healthy-Burrow ceiling, and the availability track record makes that a real gamble.

scouting_brief.prose: An elite offense (Chase and Higgins, plus offseason investment in the interior line and talk of more under-center play-action) makes him a top-10 QB when he plays. But two things cap him here: he's a pocket passer this format doesn't reward (4-point passing TDs, no rushing premium), and his availability is a genuine gamble, with significant missed time in three of the last four seasons. Health is the entire bet; the streamer band is free behind him.
scouting_brief.rationale: Elite offense makes him a top-10 QB when healthy, but he's a pocket passer this format caps (no rushing) and he's missed time in 3 of 4 years. Health is the whole bet.

scouting_brief.prose: Nominally Cleveland's WR1, but the situation is grim. He is coming off a poor 2025 (50-602-2, one of the league's worst yards-per-route marks), the Browns spent early picks on receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston (a signal they are not committed to him), and the quarterback battle between Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson and Dillon Gabriel offers no stability. A boom-or-bust WR4/flex to avoid at cost.
scouting_brief.rationale: Nominal WR1 but coming off a poor year, with drafted WR competition and a dreadful QB picture; a boom-bust WR4 to avoid at ADP.

6786.injury_history: High-ankle/shoulder issues cost games in 2025 (14); not a chronic pattern.
6786.adp_commentary: WR at ~10.3. Target hog; Pickens opposite him (now on the franchise tag, participating) is only mild competition.

scouting_brief.prose: Still the most talented WR in a pass-heavy Dallas offense (2nd in NFL passing) with Dak Prescott healthy and full scheme continuity under Schottenheimer, the setup to reclaim his 17+ PPG form after an injury-and-Pickens-hit 2025. The cap is real target competition: George Pickens drew 137 targets last year, so both can eat but Lamb's ceiling isn't the uncontested 2023 version. Locked-in Round-1 WR1.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked WR1 with Dak + continuity; Pickens target competition caps the ceiling.

scouting_brief.prose: Coming off a career-high 1,087 rushing yards and 9 TDs (a top-16 half-PPR back), but in a real timeshare: he and Kyle Monangai each played 40-60% of snaps down the stretch, and Chicago added no back. The upside lever is receiving: Ben Johnson gave him 148 targets across two years in Detroit and wants him more involved in the pass game, which could push him to RB1 territory. Elite O-line, RB2 floor, contract-year motivation.
scouting_brief.rationale: Lead back in a real timeshare with Monangai (40-60% snaps each), but Ben Johnson's scheme + elite O-line + receiving upside give an RB2 floor with RB1 upside.

6794.injury_history: 2023 hamstring (IR, soft-tissue, reinjury-prone class); durable since (17/17). Annual hamstring-flare watch.
6794.adp_commentary: WR at ~12.4. Top-3 talent; the MIN QB question (Murray/McCarthy) and the hamstring history are the only caps on an otherwise top-5 profile.

scouting_brief.prose: Uncontested target hog even in a dysfunctional 2025, so the read is the new quarterback: Minnesota added Kyler Murray to compete with (and likely beat out) second-year J.J. McCarthy, and Jefferson has stayed neutral while building chemistry with both. Analysts frame the Murray arrival as a rebound path back to the elite WR1 tier, but at least one insider tags him a risky early pick given Murray's 6.0 yards per attempt and low TD rate in 2025 plus a rushing profile that can suppress raw target volume. Talent and target share are locked; the QB resolution is the swing on his ceiling.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked target share; the Murray/McCarthy QB question is the ceiling swing, and it's broadly priced.

6797.injury_history: Durable-ish (13/17/16); no chronic pattern. New Mike McDaniel run-first scheme (quicker release, ~2.4s time-to-throw) trims pass volume.
6797.adp_commentary: QB at ~85.7. The scheme change compresses his passing volume in a format that already caps pocket QBs (4-pt TD, 1/25 yds); a streamer-band QB here unless his mobility becomes a designed-run element.

scouting_brief.prose: Real-life arrow up: new OC Mike McDaniel is overhauling his footwork and release and manufacturing easy completions, and a rebuilt line (Slater and Alt back, Strange and Biadasz added) should keep him upright, so he projects a top-10 real QB with top-five upside. For this format the translation is softer. Herbert is a pocket passer with no rushing premium, and the 4-point passing-TD scoring taxes exactly his strength, so the McDaniel efficiency bump helps less here than in standard formats. A back-end starter with a safe floor rather than a difference-maker.
scouting_brief.rationale: McDaniel's scheme and a rebuilt line lift his real value, but a pocket-passer profile in a 4-pt-pass-TD, no-rush format caps him as a back-end QB1.

6801.injury_history: Recurring soft-tissue history: hamstring (missed 2 to start a season) and a high-ankle sprain (3 games); expected 100% for Week 1. Perennial 'needs better injury luck' profile.
6801.adp_commentary: WR at ~37.8. Elite TD source (career-high 11 TDs even with Burrow hurt in 2025); the recurring soft-tissue history is the cap on an otherwise back-end-WR1 ceiling.

scouting_brief.prose: Locked No. 2 in Cincinnati's premier Burrow-led passing offense with a plush goal-line role, a career-high 11 TDs on 98 targets in 2025 (WR12). Ja'Marr Chase caps his overall target volume and takes the larger inside-the-10 share, so Higgins is a high-floor WR2 whose ceiling spikes if Chase ever misses time. The real risk is durability: he hasn't played a full season since 2020 (12 games missed over three years).
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked No. 2 with a plush goal-line role in Burrow's elite offense; Chase caps his target volume and soft-tissue durability is the recurring risk.

scouting_brief.prose: The locked Packers starter with a retooled receiver group: Christian Watson is the extended WR1 (four years, $110.5M), second-year Matthew Golden is rising into a full-time outside role, and Jayden Reed works the slot, after Green Bay moved on from Doubs and Wicks. Matt LaFleur's staff is prioritizing the Love-Golden connection in camp. A locked QB with a younger but ascending cast, and upside if Golden pops.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked GB starter with a retooled, younger WR cast (Watson, Golden, Reed); stable-to-improving outlook.

sources.label: A to Z Sports — Love embracing the new passing approach

6806.injury_history: Chronically injury-prone: long Achilles history plus a Nov 2025 foot injury that required a second opinion. gp 1/13/10 over three years. Now in a crowded Denver backfield.
6806.adp_commentary: RB at ~90.6. Talent flashes, but the availability record is among the worst on the board and the backfield is crowded (Harvey, rookie Coleman). A late-round dart, not a plan.

scouting_brief.prose: Set up as Denver's early-down lead back on a two-year, $16M deal, and he was productive in that role before getting hurt (top-five in carries and rushing yards through Week 10 of 2025). He shares the backfield with RJ Harvey (passing downs) and rookie Jonah Coleman (potential goal-line work), so it is a committee, but the early-down rushing job is his if healthy. Durability is the overriding concern: a torn ACL (2021), a torn Achilles (2023) and a season-ending foot injury (2025). A high-end flex, better in non-PPR.
scouting_brief.rationale: Denver's early-down lead when healthy, but a shared backfield and a long injury history (ACL, Achilles, foot) cap him at a non-PPR-leaning flex.

6813.injury_history: Recurring high-ankle sprains (2022 surgery, 2024 re-injury), a documented re-injury pattern; played 17 in 2025, currently healthy.
6813.adp_commentary: RB at ~6.4. Led the NFL in carries in 2025 (bell-cow volume is elite here) with the high-ankle recurrence history as the cap rather than a live concern.

scouting_brief.prose: The two-year, $44M extension settles his contract and keeps him the engine of Indianapolis's run game after a league-high 323 carries in 2025, his third 300-plus season and only the second time in six years he has played all 17. The public staff split over reducing that workload now tilts his way: RB coach DeAndre Smith wants to 'find ways to take some of that workload off him,' but Shane Steichen, who actually makes the call, answered that it is 'hard to take him off the field when he's running so good.' His pass-game role grew as well (46 catches, 378 yards on 55 targets), which lifts the half-PPR floor that pure early-down backs lack. The caps are the offense around him rather than the role: Daniel Jones is back from an Achilles tear, and the Colts lost WR Michael Pittman and right tackle Braden Smith.
scouting_brief.rationale: Extension plus Steichen's own 'hard to take him off the field' comment resolve the workload debate toward volume, which the prior brief had flagged as unresolved. A post-Achilles Daniel Jones and the losses of Pittman and RT Braden Smith are the caps.

sources.label: NFL.com (Colts aiming to take some workload off Taylor)
CBS Sports (coaching staff split on workload)

scouting_brief.prose: Traded from Indianapolis to Pittsburgh, where he is the clear WR2 opposite DK Metcalf and a natural fit as Aaron Rodgers' underneath, possession target (Rodgers threw the league's lowest average depth of target last year, and the Steelers lost his short-area guys Gainwell and Jonnu Smith). Volume and red-zone work give him a WR3 floor in a McCarthy offense that should throw more. The ceiling is limited next to Metcalf's splash plays and by Rodgers' arm. A steady value WR3.
scouting_brief.rationale: Clear PIT WR2 and a fit as Rodgers' possession target with Metcalf drawing tops; a volume-based WR3 with a capped ceiling.

scouting_brief.prose: Expected to again lead a deep Rams tight end room after career highs in 2025 (43-408-8), but the production was touchdown-fueled and low-volume (he has never averaged four targets a game), and he must fend off Tyler Higbee, second-year Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The Rams' heavy multiple-TE usage helps, but regression is likely. A high-end TE2 in a good passing game, more waiver piece than draft target.
scouting_brief.rationale: Leads a deep Rams TE room but on TD-driven, low-volume 2025 numbers with regression risk; a streamer/TE2.

scouting_brief.prose: A rushing-QB profile the format rewards, and new OC Sean Mannion (Kevin Patullo was fired) is reportedly dialing up more designed runs and pre-snap motion, aiming to get Hurts' legs back involved. That matters because his 2025 dip to eight rushing TDs (down from a 13-per-year average) drove his worst fantasy season, though he still finished QB8. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith remain, with A.J. Brown now in New England. The scheme change points his rushing-TD floor back up.
scouting_brief.rationale: New OC Mannion's designed-run emphasis should restore the rushing TDs that make Hurts a format-friendly QB; a locked role with a real bounce-back angle.

scouting_brief.prose: The Saints' clear TE1 in HC Kellen Moore's offense off a career year (77-889-3 on 103 targets with QB Tyler Shough), and the role itself is secure, but the target volume is threatened: New Orleans added Noah Fant, drafted TE Oscar Delp and spent a first-round pick on WR Jordyn Tyson. His snaps are safe; matching last year's TE-leading target share is the question, though the quality of looks in a full Kellen Moore system should rise. A locked TE1 facing a likely volume dip.
scouting_brief.rationale: Clear NO TE1 in Kellen Moore's offense, but added Fant/Delp/Tyson likely trim his career-high target volume.

SI Saints — TE position training-camp preview

scouting_brief.prose: Reunited with Mike McCarthy in Pittsburgh, where he and Jaylen Warren have been rotating first-team reps in a true committee. Dowdle brings the goal-line and early-down profile (back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons and a far better short-yardage success rate than Warren) while Warren keeps the passing-down work. One projection has him near 200 touches, 850 yards and seven TDs. An upside RB3 whose familiarity with McCarthy could earn a bigger early role, and a must-start if Warren misses time.
scouting_brief.rationale: True Pittsburgh committee with Warren; Dowdle's goal-line/early-down role and McCarthy history give upside RB3 value with a higher ceiling if Warren sits.

scouting_brief.prose: Left San Francisco in free agency and signed a one-year deal in Minnesota to be the primary slot for a Kyler Murray-led offense, working underneath alongside Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. He was the 49ers' de facto WR1 in an injury-marred 2025 (WR33) and brings a physical, chain-moving game. The target competition caps his ceiling, but the role and QB upgrade make him a late-round value in Kevin O'Connell's system.
scouting_brief.rationale: The new MIN slot in a Murray-led offense with a defined chain-moving role, but Jefferson and Addison cap the target ceiling; a late-round value.

7523.injury_history: 2024 shoulder issues (10 games); healthy 17 in 2025 under Liam Coen. No lingering concern reported.
7523.adp_commentary: QB at ~93.8. Top-10 QB upside in Year 2 of the Coen offense; the 2024 shoulder is behind him. Standard 1-QB-league caveat: streamer band is free, so pay only for the ceiling.

scouting_brief.prose: Played the best ball of his career down the stretch under first-year HC Liam Coen (26.6 fantasy points per game over his last seven), a genuine Year-2 breakout in a top-six scoring offense. He also ran for 359 yards and nine TDs, which adds format value but is the number least likely to repeat. The receiving room is loaded and crowded (Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington, Travis Hunter, plus TE Brenton Strange), so target concentration is a mild cap. A locked top-12 QB whose ceiling leans on the rushing scores holding up.
scouting_brief.rationale: Real Coen-driven breakout and a rushing element the format rewards; the nine rushing TDs are the regression risk and the WR room is crowded.

scouting_brief.prose: Undisputed Eagles WR1 after the A.J. Brown trade, working in new OC Sean Mannion's scheme, which leans on more under-center formations, motion, and throws over the middle, a shift Smith has praised directly: "he's doing a tremendous job getting everybody up to speed." Smith's own framing of the receiver room as versatile ("everybody can do everything") fits his do-it-all route tree better than a rigid X-receiver role would. The live watch is a hamstring injury that's kept him out of practice for close to a week; the team calls it not serious with no Week 1 concern, but it's worth confirming a clean return before locking in the full volume case.
scouting_brief.rationale: Clear Eagles WR1 in an under-center/motion-heavy Mannion scheme suited to his versatility; a hamstring absence nearing a week is the only near-term watch, not a role risk.

7526.injury_history: Frequent nagging (soft-tissue) injuries throughout his Miami tenure; no single structural event, but a chronic availability drag. Now in Denver.
7526.adp_commentary: WR at ~45.5. A featured role in an ascending Denver pass game is the breakout case; the chronic nagging-injury pattern is the reason he keeps hovering on the WR1 fringe rather than breaking through.

scouting_brief.prose: Featured receiver in Denver's offense under OC Davis Webb and coach Sean Payton, with Bo Nix specifically citing the explosive element the offense had "lacked for a couple years": "You just can't replace speed... he doesn't really slow down to make cuts." Nix's strongest throwing profile is on hook, pivot, and crossing routes, exactly Waddle's route-running strengths, a real scheme match rather than just a name upgrade. He was out of practice again Monday (Aug. 10) with a muscle strain, extending the chronic soft-tissue pattern from his Miami tenure that remains the standing risk on an otherwise clean WR1 fit.
scouting_brief.rationale: Explosive-play fit with Nix's hook/pivot/crossing strengths and Payton's scheme; recurring soft-tissue absences are the real risk, not a role question.

scouting_brief.prose: Signed a four-year, $52M deal to leave Jacksonville and immediately assume lead-back duties in New Orleans (Kellen Moore's offense) after an RB13 season as the Jaguars' RB1. The cap is the room: Moore said Alvin Kamara will still be 'part of the running back room,' and Kendre Miller and Devin Neal are around, so the passing-down and goal-line split is the open question. Clear early-down lead, committee-dependent ceiling.
scouting_brief.rationale: New lead back in New Orleans on a $52M deal, but Kamara staying 'part of the room' + Miller/Neal cap the pass-down and goal-line share.

7547.adp_commentary: WR at ~8.6. Volume + TD equity in a high-scoring Detroit offense; only mild target competition caps him.

scouting_brief.prose: Detroit's locked-in target hog (four straight 1,100-yard seasons and 10+ TDs in three straight) with Jared Goff still throwing. The watch is scheme continuity: John Morton was dismissed and Drew Petzing is his new (and fifth career) play-caller; St. Brown himself cautioned the offense 'won't click right away.' Talent and volume float the floor, but early-season timing is a mild question.
scouting_brief.rationale: Elite role secure; new OC Petzing + 'won't click right away' is the only drag.

scouting_brief.prose: Franchise-tagged and coming off a genuine breakout (88-928-5 in 2025), and new HC Kevin Stefanski is a strong scheme fit: his tight end finished first or second on the team in targets in four of six Cleveland seasons. The cap is quarterback uncertainty. His best 2025 stretch came with veteran Kirk Cousins (now gone), and he must build rapport with a new room where Tua Tagovailoa competes with Michael Penix (partial ACL). Drake London remains the target alpha. A top-eight TE with real ceiling if the QB play holds.
scouting_brief.rationale: Stefanski's TE-friendly scheme plus the franchise tag point up after a breakout year; QB uncertainty (Tua/Penix) is the main cap.

7564.adp_commentary: WR1 at ~3.7. Elite target share; in half-PPR his yardage/TD profile survives the reception haircut. Correctly priced top-4 overall.

scouting_brief.prose: Locked WR1 in a Bengals passing game entering OC Dan Pitcher's third year calling plays. Chase told reporters July 30 he's healthy and pushing the offense to manufacture more explosive plays (20+ yard gains) after three straight playoff misses, praising the defense's offseason additions (Dexter Lawrence, Bryan Cook, Kyle Dugger) for lifting camp energy. Zac Taylor gave him a 'maintenance' rest day Aug. 6, standard veteran-usage management with no injury attached. Higgins' 4yr/$115M re-signing keeps the receiver room's shape intact around him.
scouting_brief.rationale: Beat-confirmed healthy and voluntarily driving camp intensity; the Aug. 6 rest day was scheduled maintenance, not a health flag.

scouting_brief.prose: OC Zac Robinson has spelled out a two-back plan in Tampa: Bucky Irving as the 1A who shoulders the bulk of the carries and Gainwell as the passing-down, change-of-pace 1B, a pairing the staff runs as its "pony" package in camp. That makes Gainwell a PPR-leaning flex with a defined receiving role and clear standalone value, plus real handcuff upside if Irving (back from a 2025 shoulder issue) misses time.
scouting_brief.rationale: OC Zac Robinson's stated receiving-down 1B behind Bucky Irving; a PPR flex now and a valuable Irving handcuff.

7569.injury_history: MISSED TIME IN ALL FIVE NFL SEASONS: chronic soft-tissue availability concern. Ceiling is a Tier-1 WR if he ever plays 17.
7569.adp_commentary: WR at ~23.7. The talent says top-10 WR; the availability record says round 3. The highest injury-bust risk in the WR2 tier, a boom-or-miss-weeks pick this format's ceiling-hunting rewards, but eyes open.

scouting_brief.prose: Houston's unquestioned WR1: a third 1,000-yard season in four years and a top-10 fantasy finish in 2025, projected for 128 targets. The scheme read is neutral: OC Nick Caley's attack got a bit more conservative but pass attempts still rose, and a C.J. Stroud bounce-back is the clear ceiling-raiser (Collins actually produced without him). A potential Tank Dell return plus Higgins/Noel could make this his most crowded target room, a mild cap. Availability is his separate, well-documented risk.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked WR1; a Stroud bounce-back is the upside, a more conservative scheme + a potentially crowded room the caps (availability tracked separately).

scouting_brief.prose: Re-signed by Dallas (three years, $24M) after a 2025 breakout (252-1,201-11) and set up as the bell-cow. The Cowboys added no back in the draft, leaving only Jaydon Blue, Malik Davis and Phil Mafah behind him. The watch isn't the role, it's the trajectory: he faded from RB8 over the first half (18.5 touches, 9 TDs) to RB25 over the second (17.4 touches, 4 TDs), so his best weeks come when Dallas controls the pace.
scouting_brief.rationale: Re-signed bell-cow with no drafted threat; the watch is his 2025 second-half fade (RB8 to RB25), not the role.

scouting_brief.prose: The Week 1 favorite to lead Carolina's backfield now that Rico Dowdle left for Pittsburgh, with RotoBaller projecting 1,270 total yards and eight TDs. The case is shaky, though. He collapsed to RB40 in points per game in 2025 while fighting a calf injury and grading as one of the league's least efficient backs, and a healthy Jonathon Brooks (returning from a second ACL) plus AJ Dillon are in line to eat into the workload. A high-end RB3 with real committee risk if Brooks holds up.
scouting_brief.rationale: Week 1 lead with Dowdle gone, but 2025 inefficiency and a returning Jonathon Brooks make it a committee; an RB3 with downside if Brooks is healthy.

sources.label: RotoBaller (set to lead, Brooks mixed in)

scouting_brief.prose: Held the New England lead-back role in 2025 (57%-plus of snaps in nine of 14 games) and out-touched TreVeyon Henderson 17.8 to 8.8 in the playoffs, besting him in most efficiency metrics. This is a split, though, and the second-year Henderson is widely expected to climb the depth chart. Ball security is the swing: Stevenson has fumbled 10 times over his last 20 games, which is what could cost him touches. Best viewed as a committee lead with standalone value and league-winning upside if Henderson misses time.
scouting_brief.rationale: Held the lead over Henderson late in 2025, but it is a split and his fumbling is the risk that could flip it; committee value with handcuff-plus upside.

sources.label: RotoBaller (carve a role in split backfield)

scouting_brief.prose: Dallas's unquestioned starting tight end and Dak Prescott's top tight-end target after a four-year, $50M extension, and he has been one of the offense's standouts in camp, repeatedly connecting with Prescott on intermediate and seam throws. With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens pulling coverage, Ferguson has a clear path to career-high volume as the middle-of-field chain-mover. A locked starter whose risk is touchdown variance, not the job.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked DAL starter and Dak's top TE; Lamb/Pickens attention opens the middle, so the cap is TD variance, not role.

Blogging The Boys — Ferguson impressive in camp practices

scouting_brief.prose: Tampa Bay's clear TE1 by snaps (993 in 2025, the most at the position) with no new competition added, and Mike Evans' departure to San Francisco removes one target-hog. But the passing tree still runs through a healthy Chris Godwin, Jalen McMillan and an ascending Emeka Egbuka, plus a drafted rookie receiver, so Otton's 2025 line (59-572-1, TE22) has little room to climb. A high-end TE3 and streaming option.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked TE1 by snaps with Evans gone, but a healthy, deep TB receiver room caps his targets; a high-end TE3/streamer.

8112.injury_history: Missed games in 2025 (12); a 'Questionable' tag is carrying in Sleeper's DB. Verify at camp.
8112.adp_commentary: WR at ~17.6. Ascending target share in ATL; the Penix/Tua QB battle is the swing factor on his ceiling.

scouting_brief.prose: Locked-in WR1 and target hog (the WR6 in points per game through Week 10 last year before a PCL injury ended his season) with top-five upside if the quarterback shakes out. That's the whole question: Michael Penix Jr. has seemingly taken the lead after a Tua Tagovailoa injury but is dealing with his own camp injury, so the offense's QB is unsettled entering the season. London and Kyle Pitts both produced through shaky QB play in 2025, which is the case his talent carries the role regardless.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked WR1 target hog; the Penix/Tua QB uncertainty is the ceiling swing, and he produced through bad QB play in 2025.

scouting_brief.prose: Now the Patriots' clear No. 2 receiver after signing a four-year deal in New England and the team trading for A.J. Brown, so under QB Drake Maye he works outside and as a power slot behind Brown. A career-long outside receiver in Green Bay, Doubs gives Maye a reliable secondary target, though a Day 10 camp absence is worth monitoring. A locked WR2 whose ceiling is capped by playing second fiddle to Brown.
scouting_brief.rationale: Left GB for NE in March 2026; locked WR2 behind A.J. Brown in Drake Maye's offense, with a Day-10 camp absence to watch.

sources.label: SI On SI Patriots — depth chart entering camp
SI On SI Patriots — Top 25: don't forget Doubs

scouting_brief.prose: Now the Titans' every-down slot receiver after following OC Brian Daboll from New York, and he has already won the job outright: Cam Ward's top target through camp (team-high 26 catches, nine in one scrimmage) with rookie Carnell Tate working outside. Ward has leaned on him as a security blanket ("he really got a key to my house") and GM Mike Borgonzi made him the offense's biggest free-agent addition. A locked, high-volume slot in a young passing game; the cap is a rebuilding Tennessee offense and the TD scarcity that comes with slot work.
scouting_brief.rationale: Left NYG for TEN in March 2026; locked every-down slot and Cam Ward's top target under Daboll, so any New York framing on the board is stale.

8130.adp_commentary: TE at ~20.3. Elite target share; in a 1-TE league an every-week TE1 is worth round-2 capital given the replacement cliff, but the ARI QB uncertainty is a caveat, and rival Stipe now chases early TEs.

scouting_brief.prose: Coming off a record tight-end season (126 catches, 1,239 yards, 11 TDs) and still the locked-in centerpiece of the Arizona passing game. The QB downgrade is real (Kyler Murray is gone, with Jacoby Brissett the likely starter ahead of Minshew and Beck), and new HC Mike LaFleur's scheme should be more run-balanced. But McBride already broke out catching passes from two different QBs, and LaFleur's 12-personnel (two-tight-end) sets keep his target volume elevated even in a more balanced attack.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked elite TE target hog; QB downgrade (Murray out, Brissett in) + a more balanced scheme are offset by heavy 12-personnel usage.

scouting_brief.prose: Followed HC John Harbaugh to the Giants on a three-year, $40M deal, escaping Mark Andrews' shadow in Baltimore. He is the clear starting tight end and the No. 2 target behind Malik Nabers, and was reportedly Jaxson Dart's favorite target in spring practices, so the volume should climb. With only depth wideouts (Mooney, Slayton) behind Nabers, Likely has top-10 TE upside on a rising offense. A late-round dart with real breakout appeal.
scouting_brief.rationale: Followed Harbaugh to NYG as the clear TE1 and No. 2 target behind Nabers, with Dart chemistry; a rising-offense breakout dart.

scouting_brief.prose: Opened camp as the Cardinals' veteran early-down lead (10 first-team carries to Jeremiyah Love's four on July 29), but the rookie No. 3 overall pick has since taken over: by Aug. 9 Love ran the first three series with the starters and out-targeted Allgeier 4-1, with Arizona using Love on motion and routes while Allgeier's role stays "more static." Allgeier now profiles as the early-down and short-yardage complement, with standalone value only if Love slumps or gets hurt. Trending the wrong way as Love ascends.
scouting_brief.rationale: Rookie Jeremiyah Love took over Arizona's first-team reps by Aug 9; Allgeier is sliding to a complementary role the projection likely has not caught.

sources.label: Cardinals camp observations: Love's role expands

scouting_brief.prose: Buffalo's locked slot receiver and one of Josh Allen's most reliable targets (team-high 95 targets, 72-719-4 in 2025), but the hierarchy shifted: newly acquired DJ Moore now projects as Allen's top wideout, nudging Shakir to a clear No. 2. He is also week-to-week with a high-ankle sprain suffered in camp. A locked slot role with PPR volume, capped by Moore's arrival and the ankle.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked BUF slot, but DJ Moore's arrival bumps him to No. 2 target; a high-ankle sprain is a fresh watch.

scouting_brief.prose: Signed to own the Commanders' passing downs, where his receiving and pass-blocking give him standalone PPR value, and HC Dan Quinn singled him out as a standout of the offseason program. He shares the backfield with Jacory Croskey-Merritt (the early-down rusher) and rookie Kaytron Allen, but because Croskey-Merritt was a non-factor as a receiver, White has a clear path to three-down work if he keeps out-competing him. A committee back with the receiving role locked and a real path to the larger share.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked WAS passing-down back (Dan Quinn praise); a path to a bigger role given Croskey-Merritt's receiving limits.

notes: On the fully-guaranteed $27.3M franchise tag; attended minicamp, no holdout. Resolved.

8137.adp_commentary: WR at ~27.1. Contract-year motivation as the WR2 opposite CeeDee in Dallas; his TD-lean profile plays up in half-PPR.

scouting_brief.prose: Franchise-tagged and locked into Dallas, and the 2025 tape says he's more than a complement: with both healthy he led the Cowboys in target share (20.9%) and air-yards share (30.5%), finishing a top-6 WR (84.1 yards per game, 9 TDs) as the offense's deep-threat alpha next to CeeDee Lamb. A low-end WR1 with week-winning upside as long as he keeps his Dak Prescott chemistry; a contract-related holdout is the only real watch.
scouting_brief.rationale: Franchise-tagged and locked; the split actually favored him over CeeDee (target + air-yards leader when both healthy), a contract holdout the only mild watch.

8138.adp_commentary: RB at ~8.2. Went RB6→RB-adjacent on Brady's continuity in Buffalo; TD-dependent but the board rates him a clear value vs ADP.

scouting_brief.prose: Contract secure (4yr/$48M) as Buffalo's lead back, with Joe Brady (now HC) running the run-friendly, free-flowing style that fueled Cook's TD spike. But regression signals stack up: 16 rush TDs is unsustainable, lead blocker Reggie Gilliam left, the O-line has left-guard/tackle turnover, and DJ Moore was traded in for more target competition. Role is safe; the efficiency/TD profile is the risk the projection may carry too high.
scouting_brief.rationale: Lead-back role locked; TD regression + lost blocker + new mouths cap the upside.

scouting_brief.prose: Steps into the WR1 role after Indianapolis traded Michael Pittman Jr. to Pittsburgh, and the Colts backed him with a four-year, $114M deal. The catch is his profile: he has led the NFL in yards per reception in back-to-back years on a 16-plus average depth of target, a big-play, low-volume archetype rather than a high-target one. His ceiling rides on Daniel Jones' health and play, and he is coming off offseason ankle surgery (expected ready). A low-end WR2 with weekly variance.
scouting_brief.rationale: WR1 role and target bump with Pittman gone, but a deep, low-volume profile plus Daniel Jones at QB cap the floor; boom-bust WR2.

8144.injury_history: MAJOR RED FLAG: 4-5 diagnosed concussions (2022-2024; missed 9 games in 2024) PLUS a January-2026 blood clot in the lung, limited in offseason work. Concussion recurrence + clot is the board's most serious availability profile.

notes: Contract year in NO; hold-in chatter given health, but speculative.

8144.adp_commentary: WR at ~31.8. Pure talent is a top-15 WR, but a 4-5 concussion history plus an offseason pulmonary blood clot make this arguably the riskiest availability profile on the board. The ADP does NOT fully price the medical risk. Let someone else chase the upside.

scouting_brief.prose: The locked No. 1 target in Kellen Moore's fast-paced, aggressive offense: a 29.4% target share and a top-10 finish in 2025 that climbed once Tyler Shough settled in at QB. Scheme and role both point up, with rookie Jordyn Tyson only a minor target-cap. The dominant risk is medical: he's coming off a blood clot and carries a concussion history, though Moore says his clot recovery is clean and he's a full-go for camp.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked No. 1 target (29.4% share) in Moore's aggressive offense; the dominant risk is medical (blood clot + concussion history), not the role.

8146.injury_history: 2025 hyperextended knee (November), shut down/IR, only 7 games. One-off structural, targeting full health for 2026; not a chronic pattern.
8146.adp_commentary: WR at ~40.5. Bounce-back candidate: the knee cost 2025 but isn't chronic; the NYJ QB situation is the real cap on his rebound.

scouting_brief.prose: Unquestioned alpha (a 30% target share early in 2025 despite bad quarterback play) who now gets a real QB upgrade in Geno Smith. The two are 'cooking' in camp, and Smith has a track record of elevating his No. 1 (JSN in Seattle). First-round rookie Omar Cooper Jr. is only depth; Wilson remains the clear centerpiece with a 90/1,000 floor. The scheme/QB change is a genuine plus, more bullish than the 'QB caps him' read his discounted ADP still reflects.
scouting_brief.rationale: Unquestioned alpha now with a real QB upgrade (Geno Smith), more bullish than the standing 'QB caps him' verdict; a discounted-ADP buy.

notes: Repeat offender: 4-game gambling suspension (2023) + 2-game PED suspension (2024). A PED repeat escalates to a 17-game ban, genuine week-loss exposure. No confirmed 2026 suspension, but documented exposure per the user's 'suspension exposure' flag.

8148.adp_commentary: WR at ~52.2. Legitimate big-play, per-game upside, but the two-suspension history (especially PED, where a second strike is a full-season ban) is real exposure the ADP treats lightly. Flagged, not disqualified.

scouting_brief.prose: Finally delivered on his pedigree in 2025 (career-best 1,182 yards, a WR1 finish on a second-half surge), but the profile is fragile: a mere 17% target share and one of the highest bust rates among top-20 WRs. The 2026 headwind is scheme: new OC Drew Petzing (from Arizona) runs a more run-heavy attack with heavier personnel and fewer three-receiver sets, and with Sam LaPorta back plus St. Brown and Gibbs ahead of him, his snaps and looks could shrink. Week-winning ceiling, deeper bust risk.
scouting_brief.rationale: New OC Petzing's run-heavy, fewer-3WR-set scheme (+ LaPorta back) likely trims a low-target-share field-stretcher below the projection. Revisit.

scouting_brief.prose: Still the Rams' primary and goal-line back in McVay's scheme: 63% of the red-zone rush attempts over the second half of 2025 and three straight 15.5+ PPR seasons. The cap is a genuine and growing committee: second-year Blake Corum earned a meaningful role late, and analysts expect something closer to a 50/50 split in 2026, with Williams the between-the-tackles and third-down man. Efficiency role secure, but the touch ceiling is shrinking.
scouting_brief.rationale: Primary + goal-line role intact (63% of late-2025 RZ carries), but Blake Corum's rise toward a possible 50/50 split caps the ceiling.

8151.injury_history: Lower-body/abdomen injuries missed time 2022-24; first fully clean 17-game season in 2025. Signed with KC (new scheme) in 2026.
8151.adp_commentary: RB at ~16.8. Three straight partial seasons before 2025 plus a KC scheme change cap him; the ADP fairly bakes in the durability question.

scouting_brief.prose: Fresh three-year deal to be Kansas City's bell-cow, and Andy Reid, historically a lean-on-one-back coach (Charles, McCoy, early Hunt), appears set to hand him 15-18 carries plus goal-line work with Hunt and Pacheco gone. Clear runway in a strong RB scheme; Mahomes's presence (back from a torn ACL) keeps defenses honest. Watches: the Mahomes health question, a brand-new system, and Walker's spotty durability; one analyst calls the early 2nd-round ADP a touch rich.
scouting_brief.rationale: Bell-cow role in a back-friendly Reid scheme; Mahomes health + new system the caveats.

scouting_brief.prose: Signed with Atlanta to be the early-down and short-yardage complement behind bell-cow Bijan Robinson, filling the role Tyler Allgeier vacated by leaving for Arizona. A downhill runner who was San Francisco's No. 2 last season, he gives the Falcons a between-the-tackles change of pace, but his standalone value is limited to goal-line work and any Bijan absence. A handcuff-tier back in a Bijan-first backfield.
scouting_brief.rationale: ATL's early-down/short-yardage complement behind Bijan; value limited to goal-line and a Bijan absence.

sources.label: AtlantaFalcons.com — Falcons sign RB Brian Robinson Jr.

scouting_brief.prose: The clearest committee warning near the top of the board: HC Aaron Glenn has publicly called the backfield a 'three-headed monster' with Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis, so Hall's touches and goal-line work get siphoned off. His receiving role has already shrunk (36-350-1 on 48 targets in 2025) and his TD production is thin, even off a career-high 243-carry, 1,065-yard year. The talent is there, but the coach-declared rotation caps the ceiling below his ADP.
scouting_brief.rationale: HC Glenn's declared 'three-headed monster' (Allen, Davis) + a shrinking receiving role cap Hall well below bell-cow, a committee fade at ADP.

scouting_brief.prose: Miami's presumed Week 1 starter after Tua Tagovailoa left for Atlanta, signed to a three-year, $67.5M deal off an impressive 2025 spot start for Green Bay, but he is in a live camp competition with Quinn Ewers (who started when Tua was benched late last year). Willis's legs give him rushing-QB upside that matters in this format if he wins and holds the job. A volatile streaming QB whose value swings entirely on the Ewers battle.
scouting_brief.rationale: MIA's presumed starter after Tua's exit but in a live battle with Quinn Ewers; rushing upside if he wins, which the backup-range ADP may not price.

8167.injury_history: 20 games missed over 4 seasons, but the recurring hamstrings were tied to a biomechanical asymmetry reportedly corrected ~2 years ago, and his ACL was a 'clean' tear. Enters 2026 fully healthy for the first time in a while.
8167.adp_commentary: WR at ~63. A real breakout dart if the corrected biomechanics hold; the injury history says buyer-beware, but the cause (not just the symptom) was addressed, which is more encouraging than the raw games-missed suggests.

scouting_brief.prose: Now the clear Packers WR1 after Green Bay moved on from Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks and handed him a four-year, $92 million extension, so the target tree is finally cleared for his deep-ball efficiency. From his Week 8 return off a 2024 ACL through Week 17 he was the half-PPR WR9 (a 1,039-yard, 10-TD full-season pace). The offense still spreads it around and leans on the run, but the vacated volume points up. The one real cap is the injury history: he is only about 18 months removed from the ACL.
scouting_brief.rationale: Cleared WR room (Doubs/Wicks gone) plus a $92M extension lock him in as GB's WR1; the ACL/soft-tissue history is the standing risk, not the role.

scouting_brief.prose: Left Minnesota for a three-year, $35M deal in Las Vegas, where the Raiders want him in a more featured role as one of their top two receivers alongside Tre Tucker, behind premier target Brock Bowers. He set a career high with six touchdowns in 2024 and posted 29-444-4 in 2025, and his chemistry with Kirk Cousins puts him on the late-round radar. A deep-league flex with a genuine chance at career numbers.
scouting_brief.rationale: Signed to a featured-ish role in LV alongside Tre Tucker behind Bowers; a late-round flex with career-best upside.

8183.injury_history: 2025 missed time (9 games); cause not separately verified this pass. SF left-guard turnover (protection) is a separate 2026 risk.
8183.adp_commentary: QB at ~105.8. A pocket QB in a strong scheme, but the 2025 availability and O-line questions cap him; standard 1-QB streamer here.

scouting_brief.prose: Locked starter in Kyle Shanahan's offense and sharp in camp (24 of 28 across two team periods, with DC Raheem Morris praising his command). The weapons shifted around him: WR Ricky Pearsall is out for the season, Mike Evans was added and Christian McCaffrey is back, so the pass-catcher hierarchy is still forming. A back-end QB1 whose ceiling depends on the retooled skill group and on Shanahan's return from a July car-accident injury.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked SF starter; Pearsall out for the year, Evans in, CMC back, so the weapons reshuffle is the variable, not the job.

sources.label: SF Standard — offense adapts to Pearsall's absence

scouting_brief.prose: Left Kansas City in free agency and signed with Detroit, where he essentially replaces the traded David Montgomery as the early-down complement to bell-cow Jahmyr Gibbs. The Lions have made clear Gibbs is the workhorse, so Pacheco projects as a change-of-pace and short-yardage back with standalone flex value only in spots. A handcuff with a defined but secondary role in a good Petzing offense.
scouting_brief.rationale: Montgomery's replacement as Gibbs' early-down complement in DET; a secondary-role handcuff with spot flex value behind a bell-cow.

scouting_brief.prose: Signed with Washington (three years, $27M) for the best quarterback of his career in Jayden Daniels, in a Commanders offense that loves targeting the tight end and lacks proven pass-catchers beyond Terry McLaurin. That is a genuine scheme and QB upgrade after four years of poor Titans quarterbacking. The catch is that he has never broken out (14.9% target share in 2025), so he is a sleeper, not a lock. A late-round TE with real upside.
scouting_brief.rationale: A real QB/scheme upgrade to a TE-friendly Daniels offense thin on pass-catchers, but he has never popped; a sleeper TE with upside.

scouting_brief.prose: Listed RB1 on Pittsburgh's first depth chart (Aug 5) and coming off career highs (211 carries, 958 yards, 8 total TDs, RB18 in points per game). The role is not clean, though: new HC Mike McCarthy brought in Rico Dowdle, and the two have been splitting first-team reps in a true committee. Dowdle profiles as the goal-line and early-down back while Warren keeps the passing-down work, so his ceiling looks capped near a 50/50 split. Best valued as a high-end RB3.
scouting_brief.rationale: Opened as RB1 but McCarthy's addition of Rico Dowdle makes it a true committee (Dowdle goal-line, Warren passing downs); the split caps him at RB3 value.

scouting_brief.prose: The early-down and goal-line half of Minnesota's timeshare with Aaron Jones, and the more physical of the two. Mason ran for eight touchdowns on 36 red-zone touches in 2025 and profiles as the lead red-zone back again, with a path to pass Jones outright given the veteran's age and injury history. A rock-solid RB3 with plug-and-play RB2 upside if Jones misses time.
scouting_brief.rationale: Minnesota's early-down/goal-line back in a timeshare with Jones; standalone RB3 value with clear RB2 upside if the aging Jones sits.

scouting_brief.prose: Traded to Seattle midseason and re-signed (three years, $51M) as the clear WR2 behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, a vote of confidence that points to a bigger role. He is a downfield weapon (WR31 in 2025 across both stops) whose week-to-week output will swing with the Seahawks' run-heavy, deep-shot approach. A boom-or-bust spike-week flex at a WR58 ADP.
scouting_brief.rationale: Re-signed as SEA's clear WR2 behind JSN, but a run-heavy offense and deep-only role make him a boom-or-bust flex.

9221.injury_history: Minor 2023 (15 games), 17/17 since. No chronic pattern.
9221.adp_commentary: RB2 at ~2.9. Campbell's 'bell cow now' comments consolidate his touches (the single most valuable RB signal in this format), so a top-3 price is correct.

scouting_brief.prose: Detroit made him the highest-paid running back in NFL history (three years, $67.5M, $51M guaranteed, through 2030), which puts money behind what Dan Campbell already said out loud: 'He's going to be our bell cow now.' With David Montgomery traded to Houston the timeshare that capped his touches is gone, and the beat read on Isiah Pacheco is that he was signed as an RB2 rather than a co-starter, so this projects closer to a true workhorse load than anything Gibbs has had. Campbell has also pushed back on the space-back label ('He can create his own space in the middle'), which matters for the early-down and goal-line carries Montgomery used to absorb. Coming off 1,223 rushing yards and 18 touchdowns plus 616 receiving yards and five receiving scores, he is the ideal half-PPR back; new OC Drew Petzing is the lone unknown.
scouting_brief.rationale: Record extension plus Campbell's 'bell cow' declaration and Montgomery's exit remove the timeshare; the beat now reads Pacheco as an RB2, not a co-starter, which is a stronger role than the prior brief assumed. New OC Petzing the only unknown.
