9224.injury_history: 2023 rookie limited (12 games); 16/17 since. Trending durable.
9224.adp_commentary: RB at ~19.1. One of the board's biggest RB values vs ADP. CIN volume + a clean recent workload make him a target a full round after his value rank.

scouting_brief.prose: Locked into the top of the Cincinnati backfield in a contract year, behind an offensive line that returns all five starters. Joe Burrow endorsed him at camp as 'a close second' to Ja'Marr Chase in getting the ball, signaling continued heavy usage, with only Samaje Perine and 2025 sixth-rounder Tahj Brooks behind him. Coming off back-to-back double-digit-TD seasons; a healthy Burrow keeps the floor high and a run-leaning philosophical shift could lift the ceiling.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked lead back; Burrow calling him 'a close second' for the ball + a returning O-line and a run-leaning shift point up.

scouting_brief.prose: Traded from Jacksonville to Philadelphia, where he competes for the backup job behind Saquon Barkley. Standalone value is minimal behind a healthy Barkley (he saw about four carries a game in Jacksonville), but his efficiency is real (5.7 yards per carry in 2025), and he flashed a 106-yard game when Barkley rested. One of the best league-winning handcuffs in football if Barkley misses time.
scouting_brief.rationale: Traded to PHI as Saquon's backup; minimal standalone value but elite handcuff upside (5.7 YPC) if Barkley sits.

9226.injury_history: 2023 rookie knee (11 games); 17 then 16 since. A 'Questionable' tag is carrying in Sleeper's DB. Verify at camp, likely stale.
9226.adp_commentary: RB at ~13.6. Receiving-back volume plays slightly down in half-PPR vs full-PPR ADP, but Miami's lead role keeps him a low-end RB1.

scouting_brief.prose: Role is secure: he's the clear lead back (neither Jaylen Wright nor rookie Ollie Gordon threatened him), and OC Slowik may lean on him even harder. But the scheme signals are negative: Mike McDaniel, who built his pass-game role, is gone, and QB Malik Willis is a runner whose scrambles replace RB checkdowns and whose goal-line rushing eats Achane's TDs. Analysts already tag him a 2026 'faller.' A real receiving/TD downgrade the projection may not fully reflect.
scouting_brief.rationale: QB/scheme downgrade (Tua→Willis, McDaniel gone) likely trims his receiving + goal-line role below the projection. Revisit.

scouting_brief.prose: The Panthers picked up his fifth-year option, but this is a crossroads year: he set career highs in 2025 (3,011 yards, 23 TDs, 63.6%) yet averaged just 188 passing yards a game on 6.3 per attempt, and his three fantasy finishes are QB29, QB23, QB24. He has healthy weapons in Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker and a new play-caller (OC Brad Idzik) with more line-of-scrimmage freedom. A backup only in superflex or the deepest leagues.
scouting_brief.rationale: Career highs but a low-volume, low-ceiling passer (three straight QB23-or-worse years); a superflex-only QB despite improved weapons.

scouting_brief.prose: Jacksonville's clear TE1 for a second straight year, extended in June (three years, up to $48M) and reported to camp at 100%, working with Trevor Lawrence under new OC Liam Coen. He built his name as a blocker but posted 540 receiving yards in just 12 games in 2025, and expectations are at a career high. A locked starter whose cap is a deep pass-catcher group and touchdown volume, not his role.
scouting_brief.rationale: Extended JAX TE1 under new OC Liam Coen; role locked, the cap is target competition and TD volume.

9484.injury_history: 2025 missed time (8 games); cause not separately verified this pass. Flagged for re-check.
9484.adp_commentary: TE at ~68. An ascending GB TE; the 2025 games-missed is the availability question. A mid-round TE dart with real upside if healthy.

scouting_brief.prose: Before a 2025 ACL he was tied with Trey McBride for the TE1 overall in PPR points per game (16.2) through eight weeks, and GM Brian Gutekunst says his recovery is ahead of schedule with a Week 1 target. The situation only improved: Green Bay let Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks walk and added no notable pass-catcher, funneling targets toward Kraft. Top-three TE upside if he is at full strength early. The health timeline is the swing.
scouting_brief.rationale: Pre-injury TE1-overall pace plus a cleared GB target tree give top-3 TE upside; the ACL recovery timeline is the only real question.

scouting_brief.prose: Broke out down the stretch in 2025 (WR11 in half-PPR from Week 9 on, team leader in targets, catches and yards over that span), and OC Grant Udinski has backed him to repeat it. The problem is a genuinely crowded room: he splits Trevor Lawrence's targets with Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers and 2025 No. 2 pick Travis Hunter, so his role could be anything from a breakout WR2 to a rotational WR3. A middle-round flex whose ceiling depends on winning that competition.
scouting_brief.rationale: Strong second-half finish and coach confidence, but a crowded target tree (Thomas, Meyers, Hunter) leaves his role anywhere from WR2 to WR3.

9488.adp_commentary: WR2 at ~7.3. Led the NFL with ~44% of Seattle's air yards in 2025, format-correct here (yardage-driven, survives half-PPR). The pick your team name already endorses.

scouting_brief.prose: Unquestioned Seattle WR1 off a historic 2025 (WR2, NFL-high 36% target share, 1,793 yds), with Sam Darnold back and no new pass-catchers added to threaten his usage. The one wrinkle is scheme: OC Klint Kubiak left for Las Vegas, replaced by Brian Fleury (ex-49ers TE coach). Analysts don't expect it to tank him but flag the play-caller change. Floor is high given his first-read target dominance.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked WR1, no new target competition; the OC change (Kubiak out) is the only unknown.

9493.injury_history: 2024 PCL sprain (knee), re-aggravated from a joint practice, missed 6+; played 16 in 2025. Re-aggravation pattern is the watch.
9493.adp_commentary: WR at ~4.8. Elite when healthy; the PCL re-aggravation history plus Rams target competition cap an otherwise top-3 WR profile.

scouting_brief.prose: Locked WR1 in McVay's offense (Kingsbury joined as an assistant-HC/passing-game voice, Nate Scheelhaase holds the OC title, but McVay remains the primary play-caller) — camp reports through Aug. 5 have Nacua working exclusively with the first team, hauling in one-handed grabs on 11-on-11s and beating a Trent McDuffie pass breakup for a back-shoulder touchdown from Stafford on Aug. 3. No health concerns have surfaced in camp; the offseason rehab stint and pending legal-process McVay referenced in July haven't affected his workload. Davante Adams remains the clear goal-line/contested-catch complement (his own red-zone TD grab that same Aug. 3 practice), a real but modest cap on Nacua's touchdown ceiling even as he and Stafford build first-year chemistry together.
scouting_brief.rationale: Camp reps and Stafford chemistry (exclusive 1st-team reps, TD beating McDuffie) undercut the prior analyst 'mild drag' framing — beat evidence now backs a plus scheme fit, with Adams' goal-line role as the one remaining cap.

scouting_brief.prose: The Colts are deliberately expanding Downs' role in 2026, planning to move him off the pure slot (about 67% of his career snaps) into more outside and multi-personnel looks to get him on the field more often. GM Chris Ballard has talked up a bigger impact and the reshuffled receiver room opens targets. A slot-based complementary receiver trending up; a groin injury cost him a camp practice, worth monitoring but not reported as serious.
scouting_brief.rationale: Colts publicly planning an expanded, more-outside role; trending up from a pure slot, with a minor groin camp note.

scouting_brief.prose: A deep-threat spike-week WR (16.7 yards per catch) and a 2025 Drake Maye favorite whose 2026 outlook cratered when New England added A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs as its outside starters, pushing Boutte down the route tree to low, inconsistent volume. His name has even surfaced in trade talk tied to the Brown deal. A deep-league dart-throw at best.
scouting_brief.rationale: A deep-ball spike-week WR buried behind new arrivals A.J. Brown and Doubs in NE; low-volume, a deep-league dart.

scouting_brief.prose: Tampa Bay's No. 3 back behind the Bucky Irving / Kenneth Gainwell committee, but with a defined and valuable niche: goal-line work. He led the Bucs with seven rushing touchdowns in 2025 and handled 58% of the carries inside the five (88% after Week 12), a role his size advantage should protect or expand. A late-round sleeper whose value is almost entirely touchdown-dependent.
scouting_brief.rationale: The TB goal-line back behind Irving/Gainwell (7 rush TD, most inside-the-5 work); a TD-dependent late-round sleeper.

scouting_brief.prose: The 1B to Tony Pollard's 1A in Tennessee, valued mainly for his pass-catching (45-264 on 50 targets and real chemistry with QB Cam Ward), which gives him a PPR floor in negative game scripts. The concerns are stacking up: he has been a below-average rusher two years running, his 2025 was a 6.9-point-per-game, RB48 season, and rookie Nicholas Singleton may be the one to get lead work if Pollard misses time. A committee flex.
scouting_brief.rationale: Pollard's pass-catching complement with a PPR floor, but below-average rushing and Singleton's arrival cap him at a committee flex.

notes: Extension-leverage chatter (agent pushing for highest-paid RB) but participating; no holdout.

9509.adp_commentary: RB1 off the board at ~1.5. In a 2-RB/2-FLEX half-PPR league the elite bell-cow RB is the scarcest resource (top VORP tier), and Bijan's clean availability + workhorse role justify 1.01 cost despite Atlanta's stated wide-zone usage-cap talk.

scouting_brief.prose: The contract is settled (three years, $75M with $51M guaranteed) and he returns to a Kevin Stefanski offense built to feature him: Stefanski has coached Adrian Peterson and Nick Chubb and puts Bijan in that tier, and Tyler Allgeier's exit to Arizona leaves the goal-line work open. The 2025 profile is exactly what this half-PPR format pays for, 2,298 scrimmage yards and 11 touchdowns on a second straight 365-plus-touch season, with top-three finishes among backs in receiving yards per game, target share and yards per route run. Two mild watches, neither structural: Stefanski is ramping him back deliberately after the hold-in ('slowly get him back in there. He won't be full go'), and Brian Robinson Jr. is a genuine complement the staff has lined up alongside him rather than a pure backup.
scouting_brief.rationale: Hold-in resolved by a record-setting extension; Stefanski features him in the Peterson/Chubb tier with Allgeier's goal-line work vacated. A deliberate camp ramp-up and a capable Brian Robinson Jr. are the only watches.

A committee back whose value is touchdown- and health-dependent.

scouting_brief.rationale: Healthy again with DJ Moore opening space in Allen's offense, but shared TE snaps (Knox, Hawes) and his injury history keep him an upside TE2.

10859.adp_commentary: TE at ~78. A healthy LaPorta is a top-5 TE, but a herniated disc is the kind of injury that lingers; the ADP is a fair midpoint between his ceiling and the back risk.

LaPorta remains Detroit's clear TE1 and posted career-best efficiency (81.6% catch rate, 2.00 yards per route run) even in a nine-game, herniated-disc 2025. Positive touchdown regression is likely off just three scores. A top-eight TE with top-five upside; the durability question is the watch.
scouting_brief.rationale: Petzing's TE-friendly scheme (made McBride the TE1) plus a clear role point to a volume and TD rebound; 2025's back injury is the only watch.

scouting_brief.prose: Signed with Seattle from Green Bay and, with Zach Charbonnet (ACL) sidelined to start the year, could take the Seahawks' first carries of 2026 as the veteran in an open committee with rookie Jadarian Price and George Holani. That gives him early-season flex appeal, but no lasting floor or ceiling once Charbonnet returns and Price's role grows. A stream-early, drop-later type.
scouting_brief.rationale: Could open as SEA's early-season back with Charbonnet hurt, but Price's rise and Charbonnet's return cap him; a stream-early piece.

scouting_brief.prose: Enters Year 2 in Ben Johnson's offense with continuity and a strong environment, coming off a QB5 finish (3,942 yards, 27 TDs, 7 INTs, plus 383 rushing yards and 3 scores) that took Chicago to the divisional round. The Bears posted one of the league's best rushing success rates, and Williams' own legs add the modest floor this format rewards. His supporting cast is ascending (Rome Odunze, Luther Burden, TE Colston Loveland). Drafted around QB7, he profiles as a value with clear top-five upside.
scouting_brief.rationale: Year 2 in Ben Johnson's system after a QB5 finish, with a modest rushing floor and ascending weapons; a value at his QB7 ADP.

A locked QB with a stable-to-upgraded supporting cast and rushing-tinged upside in this format.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked DEN starter; new playcaller Davis Webb and the Jaylen Waddle trade are the only changes, both neutral-to-positive.

A backup with a defined role in a high-powered offense.

A midrange-to-low-end TE2 and bye-week filler.
scouting_brief.rationale: Darnold's primary TE and red-zone target coming off a TE14 year, but a low-volume offense and Arroyo's push cap him at a TE2.

A deep-league upside stash at a WR68 ADP.
scouting_brief.rationale: Vacated Evans targets open a WR3 role, but a serious 2025 neck injury and Year-3 availability questions make him an upside stash.

scouting_brief.rationale: DJ Moore's exit opens volume for a Year-3 breakout candidate, but a concentrated target tree (Burden, Loveland) + Caleb Williams' development cap the ceiling.

A committee WR2 with a spike-week ceiling.

A high-end WR2 outcome is the realistic upside.
scouting_brief.rationale: Coen praise plus restored Lawrence chemistry point to a bounce-back, but a crowded room (Meyers, Washington, Hunter) caps the ceiling at high-end WR2.

scouting_brief.rationale: Set to lead the Chargers in targets under WR-friendly new OC Mike McDaniel (Keenan Allen gone), a bounce-back/breakout setup.

His value is almost entirely tied to Achane's health. A late-round handcuff with real upside if Achane misses time.

The Texans have said he will "get lots of opportunities," but his standalone value sits behind Montgomery barring an injury. A committee back with pass-game usage and contingency upside.
scouting_brief.rationale: HOU RB2 behind traded-for David Montgomery (Mixon released); change-of-pace/passing role, upside on a Montgomery injury.

scouting_brief.prose: A second-year back ticketed for the third-string role in New Orleans after the Saints signed Travis Etienne and kept Alvin Kamara, both ahead of him. Projections see a modest workload (around 30 carries), so his standalone value is minimal, though backfield injuries or a short-yardage role under Kellen Moore could open a handcuff path. Deep-league stash only.
scouting_brief.rationale: Third string behind Etienne and Kamara in NO; minimal standalone value, a deep handcuff stash barring injuries.

12481.injury_history: 2025 ankle (8 games); expected full participation early in camp.
12481.adp_commentary: RB at ~44.4. NYG rookie in a possible committee under the new Harbaugh regime; ankle recovery and role split are the caps.

scouting_brief.prose: The favorite for the Giants' lead role and a bruising producer before a Week-8 ankle fracture ended his rookie year (103.8 scrimmage yards and 6 TDs over his last five games). But HC John Harbaugh says he and Tyrone Tracy are 'competing for everything' and 'both going to play a lot,' with Devin Singletary also around: a real committee, in a run-heavy Matt Nagy scheme. A low-end RB2; Tracy is the complementary pass-catching change-up.
scouting_brief.rationale: Favorite for the lead but in a real committee (Harbaugh says he and Tracy are 'competing for everything'), capping him to a low-end RB2.

scouting_brief.prose: Houston's clear WR2 next to Nico Collins after a strong rookie year (41-525-6) and a standout camp building chemistry with C.J. Stroud, drawing "future face of the franchise" praise from Collins himself. With the perimeter role opposite Collins his to lose, Higgins is set for a target bump in Year 2. A locked WR2 with real breakout upside if defenses tilt to Collins.
scouting_brief.rationale: Emerged as HOU's clear WR2 next to Nico Collins; a camp standout with Stroud, target share set to rise.

scouting_brief.prose: A second-year athlete (2025 second-rounder) coming off an efficient rookie cameo (11-231-3, a TE-best 20.8 yards per reception on a 17.6 aDOT). Sean McVay has committed to more 12- and 13-personnel in 2026 and team sources call Ferguson the centerpiece of that shift, but the Rams are deep at the position (Higbee, Parkinson, Klare) and his role is ambiguous. A monitor-list dart, undraftable outside the deepest leagues until the role clarifies.
scouting_brief.rationale: McVay's heavy-personnel shift and Ferguson's deep-ball profile are intriguing, but a crowded Rams TE room and an ambiguous role make him a monitor.

scouting_brief.prose: Carved out the passing-down role in Sean Payton's offense, who has said Harvey will 'certainly' be in position as the third-down back, a profile that fits Payton's history of featuring pass-catching backs and gives Harvey a PPR floor. He finished as a top-20 PPR back on limited early work as a rookie. The backfield is loaded, though: J.K. Dobbins is the established early-down runner and rookie Jonah Coleman projects for goal-line work, so the overall split stays unsettled. A mid-round flex with PPR-leaning value.
scouting_brief.rationale: Payton's pass-game usage gives him a PPR floor as the third-down back, but a loaded backfield (Dobbins, Coleman) keeps it a committee flex.

scouting_brief.prose: In line to lead the Jacksonville backfield after Travis Etienne left for New Orleans. Projections give him the rushing-attempt edge (roughly 197-129 over Chris Rodriguez), and HC Liam Coen has said he expects a 'big year,' praising his explosiveness. But it's a genuine three-man rotation with no clear separation (Rodriguez and LeQuint Allen), and Tuten's 3.7-yard rookie average (a below-average PFF grade) is the efficiency question. Lead-back upside, committee risk.
scouting_brief.rationale: Projected to lead the JAX backfield post-Etienne (Coen: 'big year'), but a three-man rotation with no clear separation + a 3.7-YPC rookie year cap the ceiling.

scouting_brief.prose: A second-year receiver Sean Payton has raved about (praising his hands in traffic and X-to-slot versatility), now positioned to compete for Denver's WR3 role behind Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle. His rookie year was derailed by injury, but he has carried strong camp momentum. If he wins the job and the offense improves, he is a sleeper, but it is a Franklin-versus-Bryant battle for the same snaps. A deep dynasty-and-best-ball watch.
scouting_brief.rationale: A Payton favorite battling Troy Franklin for the DEN WR3 role; upside if he wins it, but an uncertain part-time role in 2026.

scouting_brief.prose: Entered camp as the Chargers' receiving-first starting tight end off a 664-yard rookie year, but the role got crowded fast: LA signed David Njoku and added Charlie Kolar, so under HC Jim Harbaugh and new OC Mike McDaniel it reads as a three-way rotation whose snap-count margins are the whole question. Gadsden profiles as the F/receiving tight end (he added weight to answer blocking questions) and his usage is gamescript-dependent. A committee TE with TE1 upside only if he wins the receiving snaps outright.
scouting_brief.rationale: Receiving-first TE, but the Njoku + Kolar signings turned LAC's TE room into a 3-way committee; snap share is the swing.

sources.label: Chargers.com — Tre' Harris & Gadsden in McDaniel's offense
The Sporting Tribune — camp: Tre' Harris and Gadsden's rise

scouting_brief.prose: A 2025 rookie who showed some promise (44-369), but his 2026 value dimmed sharply when the Jets used a first-round pick on tight end Kenyon Sadiq, who profiles as the better pass-catcher and should absorb the short-area and seam targets. Taylor drops to a clear TE2 in a run-of-the-mill offense. A late-round stash, TE-premium at best.
scouting_brief.rationale: A promising rookie whose value fell behind first-round rookie Sadiq; a clear Jets TE2 and late-round stash.

scouting_brief.prose: Steps into a full-time outside starter role for the Packers after Romeo Doubs walked to New England and Dontayvion Wicks was traded, lining up alongside WR1 Christian Watson (and over Reed in two-receiver sets). The second-year first-rounder has been a camp standout, and the Love-to-Golden connection is a clear priority (a 50-yard Family Night touchdown). A rising starter whose target share should jump; the cap is a still-forming pecking order behind Watson.
scouting_brief.rationale: Full-time GB outside starter with Doubs/Wicks gone; camp standout, target share set to rise behind Watson.

A to Z Sports — Golden's Family Night TD

scouting_brief.prose: Sits atop the Titans' depth chart after Chig Okonkwo left for Washington, a clear promotion from a solid rookie year (44-357-2 on an 80% catch rate). His fantasy case rides on second-year QB Cam Ward taking a step under new OC Brian Daboll, in an offense that added Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson and should trend up. A best-ball value at an ADP around 174, but the unproven offense caps the floor.
scouting_brief.rationale: Clear TEN TE1 after Okonkwo's exit with an ascending offense under Daboll, but an unproven Cam Ward caps the projection; a best-ball value.

scouting_brief.prose: A 2025 rookie who barely played (28 carries, a healthy scratch late), now sitting third in Pittsburgh behind the Jaylen Warren / Rico Dowdle committee. He has no clear path to steady carries in Year 2 and should be left for dynasty leagues. The one route to relevance is an injury opening early-down work. A deep stash only.
scouting_brief.rationale: Buried behind the Warren/Dowdle committee after a nonexistent rookie year; a dynasty-only deep stash.

scouting_brief.prose: Steps into the unquestioned Cleveland TE1 job after David Njoku left for the Chargers, and new HC Todd Monken has historically been very TE-friendly (his tight end was first or second on the team in targets four times in his Cleveland years as OC). Fannin already finished around TE6 to TE8 per game as a rookie, and in five games without Njoku he averaged 15.9 PPR points. With the room cleared he could push toward 90-plus catches. The offense's shaky QB play is the main drag on the ceiling.
scouting_brief.rationale: Njoku's exit hands him the CLE TE1 role under a TE-friendly Monken staff; shaky QB play is the only real cap on top-5 TE upside.

scouting_brief.prose: McDaniel's outside-zone scheme is still a strong fit for Hampton's downhill running style, but the OC used Monday's (Aug. 10) presser to publicly disclaim a clean bell-cow role: 'I'll use all three of those guys probably every game... Good news is I see all three of those guys producing at a very high level. Bad news is I can't tell you which games those are.' He still projects Hampton for 'a ton of touches' as the early-down lead, but Vidal (pass protection) and Mitchell (explosive-play juice) both have defined weekly roles McDaniel intends to use. Fantasy analysts reacted negatively given Hampton's 2nd-round best-ball price.
scouting_brief.rationale: The OC explicitly and publicly walked back a clean-bellcow framing on Aug. 10 — a real, quotable role delta from the Aug. 8 brief that projections built before this presser likely haven't priced.

scouting_brief.prose: A dual-threat sophomore whose legs are the fantasy engine: as a rookie he rushed for 487 yards and 9 TDs and finished top-five at the position in carries inside the five, delivering eight top-10 fantasy weeks in roughly 12 starts. That rushing profile is exactly what this format rewards. He is the undisputed 2026 starter under a new staff (HC John Harbaugh, OC Matt Nagy) that likes his fit, throwing to a real WR1 in Malik Nabers. Efficiency as a passer is the developmental question, but the rushing floor makes him a strong streaming-plus QB.
scouting_brief.rationale: Rookie rushing production (487 yds, 9 TD) is the format-friendly floor, now the undisputed starter under Harbaugh/Nagy with Nabers to throw to.

12512.injury_history: 2025 leg fracture/dislocation (structural); healed on the 4-6 month timeline, expected Week 1. A 'Questionable' tag is carrying. Verify.
12512.adp_commentary: RB at ~49.6. CLE rookie in Monken's run-heavy scheme (the cycle's best RB ecosystem transplant). The healing leg is the uncertainty the ADP reflects; bwalsh89 (his 2025 stash) competes.

scouting_brief.prose: Locked primary back (he handled 79% of Cleveland's rush attempts as a rookie) with 300-touch potential in a run-heavy scheme, and he's full-go for camp after a season-ending ankle/fibula injury in Week 16. The rookie line (827 yards, 3.6 per carry) was dragged down by one of the league's worst run-blocking situations; a rebuilt O-line and any QB improvement are the path to RB2 production.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked primary back (79% of rookie-year carries) with 300-touch potential; a rebuilt O-line + QB questions are the swing on efficiency.

scouting_brief.prose: Set up to lead Tampa Bay in targets in Year 2: Mike Evans left for San Francisco, and new OC Zac Robinson has slotted Egbuka at 'Z' (comparing his instincts to Cooper Kupp) with Baker Mayfield back under center. As a rookie he went 63-938-6 with a 36.5% air-yards share before a Week-6 hamstring slowed him. Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan are the target competition; a Mayfield bounce-back is the swing on a top-10 ceiling.
scouting_brief.rationale: Evans' exit to SF opens the TB target lead; new OC Zac Robinson features him at 'Z' (Kupp comp). A breakout setup, Mayfield's bounce-back the swing.

scouting_brief.prose: Ascending featured tight end, a TE12 rookie finish (58-713-6) who was TE2 from Week 9 on, behind only McBride, in exactly the right scheme: Ben Johnson used heavy personnel at a top-5 rate (12 personnel 33%, 13 personnel 9%) and has publicly backed a 1,000-yard goal for him. Caleb Williams' developing go-to option. The only cap is a crowded, run-leaning skill room (Odunze, Burden) that limits raw target volume.
scouting_brief.rationale: Ascending featured TE (TE2 down the stretch as a rookie) in Ben Johnson's TE-friendly heavy-personnel scheme; a crowded, run-lean room the only cap.

scouting_brief.prose: A breakout TE candidate entering Year 2: his 76 catches led all rookies (76-817-4, a TE5 finish), and the target path only widened after the Colts traded away WR Michael Pittman and added no significant pass-catchers. He projects as Daniel Jones' primary target earner, so the swing is Jones' health (a late-2025 Achilles, recovery reportedly going well, expected back for Week 1). Top-5 TE with top-3 upside.
scouting_brief.rationale: Rookie TE5 now the Colts' primary target earner (Pittman traded away); top-5 TE upside, Daniel Jones' health the swing.

scouting_brief.prose: Locked in as the Bears' clear No. 2 receiver behind Rome Odunze now that DJ Moore is in Buffalo, playing in new OC Press Taylor's offense under HC Ben Johnson, an attack Taylor describes as explosiveness-first over efficiency: "I don't think Ben has ever mentioned the word efficiency. We talk about explosive." Johnson himself has been effusive in camp, saying he's "buying Luther Burden stock right now" and that the game is slowing down for the second-year receiver. A groin injury will keep him out through the preseason, but Chicago expects him back for the Sept. 13 opener, so the near-term absence reads as a discount, not a role change.
scouting_brief.rationale: Clear No. 2 in an explosive, Ben Johnson-designed scheme with both the OC and HC praising his growth; the groin injury is a short-term discount, not a role risk.

scouting_brief.prose: The 2025 No. 1 overall pick had a rough rebuild-year rookie season (3,169 yards, 15 TDs, under 60% completion, a league-high 55 sacks), but the arrow points up. New OC Brian Daboll has a track record with mobile QBs and is expected to give Ward more designed runs and freedom to scramble, and the Titans added Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson and interior line help. He rarely used his legs as a rookie, so the rushing floor is a projection, not a given. A high-upside QB3 to stash, not start.
scouting_brief.rationale: Ascending under Daboll with new weapons and a possible rushing bump, but a rough rookie year and unproven legs keep him a QB3 stash.

scouting_brief.prose: The clear, uncontested Carolina WR1: the 8th pick in 2025 who posted 122 targets, 1,014 yards and AP Offensive Rookie of the Year as a rookie, with no meaningful target competition added (only unproven Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette beside him). The second-year case is a Bryce Young Year-4 leap plus added offensive-line help and a vertical complement; the room to grow is real on an already-1,000-yard floor. Contested-catch polish is the on-field thing to clean up.
scouting_brief.rationale: Locked, uncontested WR1 (no target competition added); a Bryce Young leap + OL help are upside on a 1,000-yard rookie base.

12527.adp_commentary: RB at ~11.9. Projected rookie workhorse in LV. No availability history to lean on, so the projection carries all the weight; rookie variance applies.

scouting_brief.prose: Clear scheme upgrade: Chip Kelly is out as OC, and Klint Kubiak's system (81+ backfield receptions/yr since 2021) plus a rebuilt line (added C Tyler Linderbaum) point to three-down workhorse usage. RB coach says he's 'doing all the right things' for a full workhorse role; 4th-round rookie Mike Washington is only a pusher. Consensus bounce-back from a disappointing RB16 rookie year to top-10 upside.
scouting_brief.rationale: Workhorse + Kubiak pass-game usage + better scheme/OL; only a late-round pusher behind him.

scouting_brief.prose: A dynamic Year-2 back (911 rushing yards, 9 TDs, 5.1 per carry, plus 35 catches as a rookie) with real breakout upside in a run-heavy Patriots approach, but not a clean lead: he and Rhamondre Stevenson split 310 carries in 2025, Stevenson (trusted as the downhill runner and signed through 2028) isn't going away, and the committee is expected to continue. Safe as a flex with RB2 upside if he seizes the lead role, capped if the split holds.
scouting_brief.rationale: Explosive Year-2 back with breakout upside, but a continued split with Rhamondre Stevenson (signed through 2028) caps a clean lead role.

scouting_brief.prose: Playing both ways for Jacksonville, but through 10 camp days he has logged more defense than offense (88 defensive snaps to 55 on offense), and the staff plans to lean him toward cornerback given the team's receiver depth. He flashes elite ball skills on offense (an interception and a 35-yard catch within three plays on his best day), but his fantasy value is capped by a receiver snap count that is the secondary half of a two-way role. A boom-play WR whose volume is the open question.
scouting_brief.rationale: JAX two-way player logging more defense than offense (88-55); CB-leaning usage caps his WR volume despite elite flashes.

Heavy — camp notes settle Hunter's primary role

scouting_brief.prose: Washington is pushing Croskey-Merritt to be its lead, early-down back in 2026 and wants him to grow into an "every-down" role, but the room is crowded: they signed Rachaad White (third-down/passing), Jerome Ford, re-signed Jeremy McNichols and drafted Kaytron Allen (short-yardage). He added eight pounds and is working to answer pass-catching questions, which are the swing between a committee flex and a real workload. A committee back leading the early-down snaps, with standalone value that climbs if the receiving work comes.
scouting_brief.rationale: Washington's early-down lead in a crowded RBBC (White, Ford, Allen); every-down upside hinges on his pass-catching.

scouting_brief.prose: Emerged into a near-even timeshare with D'Andre Swift late in 2025 (neither back outside a 41-59% snap range from Week 12 on) in what should be a strong Ben Johnson running game behind a good line. Monangai is the more physical downhill runner and could grow into more early-down and goal-line work in Year 2, and Swift is on an expiring contract. An RB3/flex with real handcuff value: if Swift misses time, Monangai is an every-week starter.
scouting_brief.rationale: Near-even late-season split with Swift in a strong Ben Johnson run game; a physical downhill profile gives standalone flex value plus league-winning handcuff upside.

scouting_brief.prose: A 2025 rookie who made his mark as an All-Pro kick returner (48-423-4 on offense), but his offensive outlook is trending down after Tennessee's aggressive receiver moves: Carnell Tate (No. 4 pick), Wan'Dale Robinson and a returning Calvin Ridley now sit ahead of him. He is competing just for the No. 3 or even No. 5 role in a young Cam Ward offense. Roster him for special teams, not fantasy offense.
scouting_brief.rationale: Buried by TEN's WR additions (Tate, Wan'Dale, Ridley) into a WR4/5 fight; an All-Pro returner with negligible fantasy-offense value.

scouting_brief.prose: New Orleans has committed to him as the 2026 starter, and the second-year QB earned it: he was QB12 in points per game from Week 9 on with 17-plus fantasy points in each of his last six starts. Kellen Moore's fast-paced offense (top-five in plays per game) should feed him attempts, and the weapons improved (Chris Olave, rookie Jordyn Tyson, Travis Etienne, TE Juwan Johnson). A pocket passer, so the format caps the ceiling, but a genuine late-round upside dart.
scouting_brief.rationale: Committed starter coming off a QB12 finish in a fast-paced Moore offense with improved weapons; a late-round upside QB the format still caps.

scouting_brief.prose: The No. 1 overall pick (Indiana, a Heisman winner off a 16-0 national title), but he opens 2026 as the Raiders' QB2 behind veteran Kirk Cousins, so his redraft value is minimal. He is a tactical scrambler rather than a rushing threat, which caps his format upside even if he starts. A dynasty centerpiece, but a stash-only rookie for 2026 unless Cousins falters.
scouting_brief.rationale: No. 1 overall pick opening behind Kirk Cousins in LV; a dynasty asset but a redraft stash with limited rushing upside in 2026.

scouting_brief.prose: The Rams' first-round pick (No. 13, Alabama) and the heir to 38-year-old Matthew Stafford, who is under contract for one more year. Simpson is not expected to play in 2026 barring a Stafford injury, so he has no redraft value, but he landed in an ideal Sean McVay situation for the long term. A dynasty asset, not a 2026 fantasy consideration.
scouting_brief.rationale: A first-round rookie sitting behind Stafford in an ideal McVay landing spot; no 2026 redraft value, a dynasty stash.

scouting_brief.prose: A rookie (Indiana product, 69-937-13 as a college WR1) into a Jets offense that lacks an established No. 2 behind Garrett Wilson, and his run-after-catch game and inside-outside flexibility give him a real path to that role over time. The cap is the setting: the Jets offense has held back even Wilson, and he shares targets with Wilson and rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq. A backend WR5 with sleeper upside at his ADP.
scouting_brief.rationale: Rookie with a path to the Jets' open WR2 role behind Garrett Wilson, but a poor offense and shared targets cap the immediate outlook.

scouting_brief.prose: A top-five rookie WR (4th overall to Tennessee) with a path to becoming the Titans' target leader in new OC Brian Daboll's offense (HC Robert Saleh), paired with ascending second-year QB Cam Ward. An elite route runner (10th in YPRR, 4th in receiving grade in college), he projects around 86-990-6. The rookie caveat is a real target hierarchy to sort: Calvin Ridley and Wan'Dale Robinson are also in the room, so the No. 1 role is not handed to him yet.
scouting_brief.rationale: Top-five rookie WR with a path to the Titans' target lead in Daboll's offense (HC Robert Saleh), but Calvin Ridley + Wan'Dale Robinson leave the rookie target hierarchy unsettled.

scouting_brief.prose: The No. 8 overall pick and consensus top rookie WR, slated as an immediate Week 1 starter opposite Chris Olave with little other target competition (Devaughn Vele, Ja'Lynn Polk). His college profile is elite: a 31.2% career target-per-route rate and top-five marks in first downs per route run, winning at all three levels. He plays second fiddle to Olave to start, but the path to a real share in an ascending offense under second-year QB Tyler Shough is clear. Rookie target-hierarchy uncertainty is the only check.
scouting_brief.rationale: Immediate Week 1 starter opposite Olave with little competition and an elite college profile; only the usual rookie target-share ramp is the check.

scouting_brief.prose: A rookie with one of the best landing spots in the class (32nd overall): Kenneth Walker left for Kansas City and Zach Charbonnet opens the season hurt, so Price has a clear runway at 15-20 touches a game with real home-run ability. Analysts call him a top rookie-RB breakout on landing spot alone. The check is that camp is still an unsettled committee (George Holani and Emmanuel Wilson competing), so the lead role isn't locked yet.
scouting_brief.rationale: Golden landing spot (Walker left for KC, Charbonnet hurt early) with 15-20-touch upside, but a camp committee with Holani/Wilson isn't settled.

notes: Rookie: not individually vetted; low draft-decision priority.

13287.adp_commentary: Projected ~RB7 at ADP ~17.1, but a rookie with no NFL availability data (shows 'no data'). Value is projection-only. Treat with full rookie variance.

scouting_brief.prose: The No. 3 overall pick, drafted into a Cardinals backfield HC Mike LaFleur calls plays for (with Nathaniel Hackett as OC) in a run-balanced scheme that suits a workhorse. Camp usage is now backing the fit up: Sunday (Aug. 9) was Love's most involved day yet, taking the first-three-drives starter reps over veteran Tyler Allgeier for the first time and out-targeting him 4-to-1, though carries stayed close (Allgeier 7, Love 5). QB Jacoby Brissett has been effusive ('I see why we paid him $50M, that's for sure'), and LaFleur frames playing-time decisions as a 'collective, communicative effort' rather than a fixed plan. James Conner (foot surgery recovery) still hasn't worked into 11-on-11s, leaving Allgeier as the only real on-field competition right now.
scouting_brief.rationale: Aug. 9 practice reps favored Love over Allgeier on early-down snaps and targets for the first time this camp — a fresh, camp-specific signal that projections built on the earlier 'committee' framing likely haven't caught up to.

scouting_brief.prose: A fifth-round rookie into a good landing spot but a crowded present, sitting third on the Titans' depth chart behind Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears, with a chance to be Pollard's direct backup by Week 1. His clearest path to snaps is as a pass-catcher (already the team's best receiving back), but he likely needs an injury to reach a meaningful role. A high-ceiling, no-floor late-round stash.
scouting_brief.rationale: Rookie behind Pollard and Spears with pass-catching appeal, but needs an injury for real snaps; a no-floor late stash.

scouting_brief.prose: The No. 20 pick and 2025 Biletnikoff winner (79-1,156-11 at USC), a polished slot receiver who wins after the catch. The A.J. Brown trade to New England opened a starting-caliber role, but this is still Philadelphia's deepest receiver room in years (DeVonta Smith plus a run-leaning, Saquon-anchored offense under new OC Sean Mannion), so a rookie target share is hard to project. Consensus lands him around WR28 (roughly 71-902-5). The talent is there; opportunity in a crowded, run-first offense is the question.
scouting_brief.rationale: Elite college profile and the Brown trade open a role, but a deep WR room and run-leaning Eagles offense make the rookie target share uncertain.

scouting_brief.prose: The Browns' first-round rookie (No. 24), a quick, explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose 27.2% college target share topped this draft class (61-919-9 at Texas A&M). He steps into a real opening for slot and underneath work, but the setting is the drag: Cleveland's quarterback situation is unsettled and he shares targets with Jerry Jeudy and TE Harold Fannin. A rookie with talent and a role to win, but a murky, low-floor projection this year.
scouting_brief.rationale: First-round rookie with an elite college target share and a slot opening, but a shaky CLE QB picture and target competition keep the rookie projection murky.

scouting_brief.prose: A third-round rookie (No. 71, Clemson) into an immediate slot role for Jayden Daniels, in a Washington receiver room that is thin behind Terry McLaurin. His slot-driven, volume-earning profile fits, and there is a path to becoming Daniels' primary underneath target, though the Stefon Diggs signing and Luke McCaffrey are competition. An upside WR3 dart for a rising offense.
scouting_brief.rationale: Rookie with an immediate slot path for Daniels in a thin WR room, but Diggs and McCaffrey compete; an upside WR3 dart.

scouting_brief.prose: A fourth-round rookie (Arkansas) and the primary backup to Ashton Jeanty in Las Vegas, with elite athletic testing (a perfect Relative Athletic Score, 4.33 speed) and real receiving chops (28 catches in college). He could handle early-down relief and profiles as one of the better handcuffs in the league, but standalone value requires a Jeanty absence. A late-round lottery ticket.
scouting_brief.rationale: Elite-athlete rookie backing up Jeanty in LV; a premium handcuff whose standalone value needs a Jeanty injury.

scouting_brief.prose: A first-round rookie (No. 16) with rare athleticism and movable-chess-piece upside, and he has reportedly climbed ahead of Mason Taylor on the Jets depth chart. The situation is the problem: the Jets offense has capped even Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall, and Sadiq shares targets with Wilson, rookie WR Omar Cooper and Taylor. Priced around TE20 with top-10 traits but a TE33-type floor. A traits bet in a poor offense.
scouting_brief.rationale: First-round athlete climbing the Jets depth chart, but a poor offense and shared targets (Wilson, Taylor, Cooper) leave a wide range; a traits bet.

scouting_brief.prose: A fifth-round rookie into a reshaped Kansas City backfield, currently fourth in the pecking order behind Kenneth Walker, Emari Demercado and Brashard Smith. His profile is genuinely fantasy-friendly (1,451 rushing yards and 46 catches in his final Nebraska season, a dual-threat with real athletic testing), and the Chiefs were thrilled to land him, but the depth chart caps 2026 redraft value. A deep dynasty stash more than a redraft target.
scouting_brief.rationale: Dual-threat rookie profile the models like, but fourth on the KC depth chart behind Walker; a dynasty stash with minimal 2026 redraft value.

scouting_brief.prose: A Broncos rookie (fourth round, Washington) competing with RJ Harvey for the complementary snaps behind starter J.K. Dobbins, and he has flashed: HC Sean Payton praised him ("you don't feel a rookie, he's playing") and he had camp's best run by any back in a padded session. Payton favors a committee, so Coleman could carve out third-down and change-of-pace work in Year 1. A deep-league dart whose role depends on beating out Harvey and any Dobbins absence.
scouting_brief.rationale: DEN rookie battling RJ Harvey for the complementary role behind Dobbins; Payton praise, committee upside if he wins snaps.

SI On SI Broncos — Coleman earning all-rookie buzz

scouting_brief.prose: A Browns second-round rookie (No. 39, out of Washington) who has been camp's biggest surprise, catching three touchdowns in one practice and earning a first-team promotion from HC Todd Monken. The 6-4 target wins contested balls, but Cleveland's receiver room is deep and unsettled and the quarterback situation is shaky, so his Week 1 role is not yet defined. A high-upside rookie dart whose snaps are trending up but not locked.
scouting_brief.rationale: CLE 2nd-round rookie, camp standout with a first-team promotion (Monken), but a deep WR room and shaky QB cap his defined role.

scouting_brief.prose: A second-round rookie (No. 54, Vanderbilt, the John Mackey Award winner) with elite athletic testing, but he is a clear No. 3 tight end in Philadelphia behind Dallas Goedert and blocking specialist Johnny Mundt. He projects as a jumbo-slot part-timer whose blocking needs work, and a minicamp leg injury slowed him. His fantasy path really opens only when Goedert moves on (possibly 2027). Avoid in redraft.
scouting_brief.rationale: Athletic rookie but the No. 3 PHI TE behind Goedert; a redraft avoid whose window opens only post-Goedert.

scouting_brief.prose: A sixth-round rookie (Penn State's all-time leading rusher, ahead of Saquon Barkley) into a wide-open Washington backfield, where he splits work with Jacory Croskey-Merritt and passing-down back Rachaad White. He is a durable, decisive between-the-tackles runner but not a burner and a limited pass-catcher, so his ceiling is checkdown and early-down work. On the deep-league radar with a path to the No. 3 role if he impresses in camp.
scouting_brief.rationale: Productive rookie runner in an open WAS committee (CM, White), but limited as a receiver; a deep-league radar back.

scouting_brief.prose: A second-round rookie (No. 33, Ole Miss) into a Kyle Shanahan offense that needed receivers, with 4.36 speed and strong yards-after-catch production. His path widened when Ricky Pearsall suffered a season-ending knee injury, so notable rookie snaps are in play behind WR1 Mike Evans, though he still competes with Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk. One of the widest ranges of outcomes in the class: league-winning upside or a healthy scratch. A late-round dart.
scouting_brief.rationale: Rookie speed into a Shanahan offense with Pearsall hurt opening snaps, but a crowded WR2 competition (Deebo, Kirk) leaves a very wide range.
